items.description: Every resource must carry at minimum the Owner, CostCenter, and Environment tags, populated with valid values from the enterprise reference data. These tags underpin cost allocation, incident routing, and lifecycle decisions, and missing or invalid tags are reported for remediation.

items.name: Reserved Instances for Steady-State Workloads
items.description: Workloads with stable, predictable demand, such as core policy administration and claims systems, must be covered by reserved instances or savings plans rather than on-demand pricing. Commitment levels are reviewed against the application roadmap so reservations are not purchased for systems slated for retirement or migration.

items.name: Resource Tagging for Cost Allocation
items.description: Every provisioned cloud resource must carry the mandatory cost-allocation tags so that spend can be charged back to the owning business unit, product line, or transformation initiative. Untagged resources are flagged by policy and remediated within the billing cycle, keeping showback and chargeback reports accurate for P&C, Life & Retirement, and group benefits workloads.

items.name: Standard Naming Pattern {env}-{region}-{app}-{resource}-{instance}
items.description: Resources are named using the mandated pattern of environment, region, application, resource type, and instance, using the approved abbreviation lists for each segment. The convention is enforced through provisioning policy so non-conforming names are rejected before deployment.

items.name: Standard Subscription Structure
items.description: Subscriptions and accounts are organized according to the enterprise hierarchy, separating production from non-production and aligning to business domains and management groups. New subscriptions are vended through the standard process rather than created ad hoc, preserving consistent governance scopes.

items.name: Terraform Preferred or Bicep
items.description: Infrastructure definitions must be authored in Terraform as the preferred tool, with Bicep accepted for Azure-native teams. Other provisioning tools require an Architecture Review Board exception, and modules should be drawn from the shared, certified module library where one exists.

items.name: All Datasets Registered
items.description: Every production dataset, including warehouse tables, lake assets, and key application extracts, must be registered in the enterprise data catalog before it is consumed by downstream users. Unregistered data sources are not approved for reporting or model development.

items.name: Automated Discovery Preferred
items.description: Lineage should be harvested automatically from pipelines, SQL, and orchestration metadata wherever tooling permits, with manual documentation reserved for gaps the scanners cannot reach. Manually maintained lineage must identify an owner responsible for keeping it current.

items.name: Automated Profiling
items.description: Datasets are profiled on an automated schedule, with quality rules executed in pipelines rather than through periodic manual checks. New sources are profiled before onboarding so structural surprises are caught ahead of production use.

items.name: Business Glossary Linked
items.description: Catalog entries are linked to business glossary terms so technical assets are explained in the carrier's own vocabulary, such as written premium, incurred loss, and in-force policy. Glossary terms are owned by business stewards and changes follow the glossary governance process.

items.name: Conceptual, Logical, and Physical Models Required
items.description: Significant data initiatives must produce models at all three levels of abstraction: a conceptual model agreed with the business, a logical model defining entities and relationships, and a physical model reflecting the implemented schema. Each level is reviewed at the appropriate design gate.

items.name: DQ Scores Published
items.description: Quality scores for governed datasets are published to the data catalog and steward dashboards, making fitness-for-purpose visible to consumers before they build on a dataset. Trends are reviewed by the data governance forum to direct improvement effort.

items.name: Data Contracts Enforced
items.description: Interfaces between producing and consuming teams are governed by explicit data contracts specifying schema, semantics, quality expectations, and delivery cadence. Contract changes follow a versioned, communicated process so downstream actuarial and reporting consumers are never broken without notice.

items.name: ELT Preferred for Cloud
items.description: On cloud analytics platforms, pipelines should load raw data first and transform within the target platform, exploiting its scalable compute and preserving the unmodified source for reprocessing. Traditional ETL patterns are reserved for cases with a documented justification, such as in-flight masking requirements.

items.name: ERD in Approved Tool
items.description: Entity-relationship diagrams must be authored and maintained in the enterprise-approved modeling tool rather than ad hoc drawing applications, so models remain versioned, shareable, and connected to the metadata repository. Exported snapshots in documents are reference copies only.

items.name: End-to-End Lineage Captured
items.description: Lineage must be recorded from originating systems, such as policy administration and claims platforms, through integration and transformation layers to final consumption in reports, dashboards, and models. Critical regulatory and financial reporting flows are prioritized for full coverage.

items.name: Golden Records for Customer, Policy, Claim, and Product
items.description: Authoritative golden records are maintained for the Customer, Policy, Claim, and Product domains, with defined survivorship rules determining which source attributes win when systems disagree. Consuming applications and analytics draw these entities from the mastered source rather than reconciling them locally.

items.name: Governed Self-Service
items.description: Analysts may build their own datasets and reports within sanctioned workspaces, using cataloged sources and subject to access controls and certification before broad sharing. Self-service content that becomes business-critical must be promoted into managed, supported assets.

items.name: Idempotent Pipelines
items.description: Pipelines must be safe to re-run without producing duplicates or corrupting state, using techniques such as merge logic, deterministic keys, and watermarking. This allows failed loads of policy, claims, or billing data to be replayed during incident recovery without manual cleanup.

items.name: Lineage Published to Catalog
items.description: Captured lineage is published into the enterprise data catalog so analysts and auditors can trace any asset's upstream sources and downstream consumers from a single interface. Lineage views are kept synchronized with pipeline changes through the deployment process.

items.name: MDM Hub for Cross-Domain Resolution
items.description: A central MDM hub performs matching, merging, and identity resolution across source systems and business lines, linking, for example, a household's P&C policies with their life and retirement holdings. Match rules and thresholds are governed, and steward workflows handle records the engine cannot resolve automatically.

items.name: Medallion Architecture (Bronze/Silver/Gold)
items.description: Analytics platforms organize data into Bronze raw, Silver conformed, and Gold consumption layers, with defined quality and transformation expectations at each tier. Consumers such as pricing models and regulatory reports draw from Gold, while data engineering work progresses data through the layers under version control.

items.name: Naming Conventions Enforced
items.description: Entity, attribute, table, and column names follow the published enterprise naming standards, including approved abbreviations and class words. Conformance is checked at model review and through automated schema linting where available, preventing divergent vocabularies across the data estate.

items.name: Quality Rules Defined
items.description: Each critical data element carries documented quality rules covering dimensions such as completeness, validity, accuracy, and timeliness, agreed with the data steward and the consuming business areas. Rules are versioned and traceable to the business requirement they protect.

items.name: Remediation SLAs
items.description: Quality defects are triaged by severity and remediated within defined service levels, with breaches of SLA on critical elements escalated to the owning steward and domain leadership. Root-cause fixes at the source system are preferred over repeated downstream cleansing.

items.name: Schema Evolution Handled
items.description: Pipelines must tolerate additive source schema changes without failure and detect breaking changes explicitly rather than silently dropping or corrupting fields. Schema change handling behavior is documented per pipeline and validated in testing.

items.name: Searchable Metadata
items.description: Technical and business metadata, including schemas, descriptions, classifications, and quality indicators, must be populated and indexed so users can locate assets by keyword, domain, or term. Sparse or stale metadata is treated as a catalog quality defect and remediated by the steward.

items.name: Semantic Layer for BI
items.description: Business intelligence tools connect through a governed semantic layer that defines certified measures, dimensions, and business logic once, including insurance-specific calculations like loss ratio and earned premium. This prevents divergent metric definitions from appearing across departmental dashboards.

items.name: Stewardship Assigned
items.description: Each cataloged asset has a named data steward and owning domain accountable for its definition, quality, and access decisions. Stewardship assignments are kept current as organizational changes occur, so no critical dataset is left without an accountable party.

items.name: C4 Model (Context, Container, Component, Code)
items.description: Architecture diagrams follow the C4 model, presenting systems at the Context, Container, Component, and where useful Code levels of zoom. Each solution design includes at minimum the Context and Container views so reviewers can see both the business landscape and the deployable structure.

items.name: Confluence for Documentation
items.description: Narrative architecture documentation, including solution designs, decision records, and standards, resides in the enterprise Confluence space using the approved page templates. Documentation scattered in personal drives or email does not count as the system of record.

items.name: Draw.io or LucidChart
items.description: Diagrams are produced in draw.io or LucidChart, the two approved tools, using the shared enterprise shape libraries and templates. Restricting tooling keeps diagrams editable by any architect and avoids stranded artifacts in unsupported formats.

items.name: Git for Diagrams-as-Code
items.description: Diagrams expressed as code, such as PlantUML, Mermaid, or Structurizr definitions, are stored in Git repositories where they can be reviewed, versioned, and rendered in pipelines. This keeps machine-readable architecture artifacts adjacent to the systems they describe.

items.name: Non-Functional Requirements
items.description: Every project must capture its non-functional requirements as a formal deliverable, documenting expectations for performance, scalability, availability, security, and compliance before design is approved. This ensures qualities critical to an insurance carrier, such as regulatory compliance and peak-season resilience, are engineered in from the start rather than discovered as gaps in production.

items.name: Operational Runbooks Required Before Go-Live
items.description: No system enters production without runbooks covering startup and shutdown, health checks, common failure modes, escalation paths, and recovery procedures. Runbook completeness is a gate in the production readiness review.

items.name: PlantUML or Mermaid
items.description: Diagrams are authored in PlantUML or Mermaid text notation rather than drawing tools, so they can be diffed, reviewed in pull requests, and rendered automatically in documentation sites.

items.name: Required for Complex Flows
items.description: Sequence diagrams must be produced for flows involving multiple services, asynchronous messaging, or intricate error handling, such as claims intake spanning core systems, payment, and correspondence platforms. Simple single-service request paths do not require one.

items.name: Reviewed Quarterly
items.description: Each runbook is reviewed at least quarterly by the owning team and updated to reflect architectural, tooling, and procedural changes, with the review date recorded on the document. Runbooks found inaccurate during an incident trigger an immediate out-of-cycle update.

items.name: Searchable and Maintained
items.description: Repository content must be organized and labeled so material is discoverable by search, and owners review their pages on a defined cadence to archive or update stale content. Pages without a current owner or review date are flagged during periodic repository hygiene sweeps.

items.name: Stored in Wiki
items.description: Runbooks are published in the enterprise wiki at the standard location for the owning service, linked from monitoring alerts where possible, and accessible to on-call staff at all hours. Copies held only in local files or chat threads do not meet the standard.

items.name: Stored with Code
items.description: Sequence diagram sources live in the repository of the service whose behavior they describe, and updates accompany the code changes that alter the flow. Keeping the diagram in the same change set prevents documentation from drifting behind the implementation.

items.name: Version Controlled
items.description: Diagram source files are stored under version control alongside or referenced from the owning system's repository, so changes are attributable and earlier states recoverable. Static image exports without an editable, versioned source do not satisfy the standard.

items.name: AKS (Kubernetes) for Container Orchestration
items.description: Production container workloads run on Azure Kubernetes Service clusters provisioned through the enterprise landing zone, inheriting standard policies for networking, identity, and admission control. Teams deploy onto shared or dedicated AKS clusters per the platform team's tenancy model rather than operating their own orchestrators.

items.name: Artifactory for Artifacts
items.description: All build artifacts, container images, and third-party dependencies are stored in and resolved from Artifactory, providing a single controlled supply chain with vulnerability scanning and immutable release versions. Pulling dependencies directly from public registries in production builds is prohibited.

items.name: Azure API Management for API Gateway
items.description: All APIs exposed beyond their owning team are published through Azure API Management, which provides the standard policies for authentication, throttling, versioning, and analytics. Direct consumer connections that bypass the gateway are not permitted for shared or external-facing APIs.

items.name: Azure DevOps or GitHub Actions for Pipelines
items.description: Build and deployment pipelines run on Azure DevOps or GitHub Actions, using the shared enterprise pipeline templates that embed security scanning and approval gates. Self-hosted or unsanctioned CI systems are not permitted for code that reaches production.

items.name: Azure Monitor and Dynatrace for APM
items.description: Application performance monitoring is delivered through Azure Monitor for platform-level telemetry and Dynatrace for deep application tracing and dependency mapping. Production services must emit telemetry into this stack, instrumented to the enterprise standard, before go-live.

items.name: Azure Primary, AWS Secondary for Specific Workloads
items.description: Microsoft Azure is the default platform for new workloads, where the enterprise landing zones, identity integration, and operational tooling are most mature. AWS is sanctioned only for the specific workload categories where it is the established or superior fit, as documented in the platform selection guidance.

items.name: Azure Service Bus and Kafka for Event Streaming
items.description: Azure Service Bus is the standard for enterprise queuing and pub-sub command-style messaging, while Kafka serves high-volume event streaming such as telematics feeds, claims event propagation, and integration event backbones. Teams select between them based on documented pattern guidance rather than preference.

items.name: Docker for Local Development
items.description: Developers use Docker for building and running containers locally, working from the approved base images maintained by the platform team. Local images must be rebuilt from the same Dockerfiles the pipeline uses, keeping development parity with what ships to AKS.

items.name: Exceptions Require ARB Approval
items.description: Use of any other language, or of an approved language below its minimum version, requires a documented exception approved by the Architecture Review Board. Approvals record the justification, scope, and expiry so exceptions are revisited rather than becoming permanent.

items.name: Grafana for Dashboards
items.description: Operational dashboards are built in Grafana against the approved telemetry sources, using shared templates for service health views. Each production service maintains at least a standard golden-signals dashboard accessible to its support team.

items.name: GraphQL for BFF Patterns
items.description: Backend-for-frontend layers serving web and mobile experiences may use GraphQL to aggregate multiple downstream services into channel-shaped queries. GraphQL is scoped to the BFF tier and is not the standard for service-to-service or system-of-record APIs.

items.name: Helm for Packaging
items.description: Kubernetes applications are packaged and released as Helm charts following the enterprise chart conventions for values, secrets references, and resource limits. Charts are versioned and published to the artifact repository so deployments are repeatable across environments.

items.name: Java 17+, Python 3.10+, TypeScript/Node.js 18+, C# .NET 6+
items.description: New development uses Java 17 or later, Python 3.10 or later, TypeScript on Node.js 18 or later, or C# on .NET 6 or later. The version floors ensure supported runtimes with current security patching, and existing systems below these versions carry upgrade plans on their technology roadmaps.

items.name: MongoDB for Document Stores
items.description: Where a document model genuinely fits, such as flexible product configuration or content-style payloads, MongoDB is the approved document database. Teams must justify the document model choice at design review rather than defaulting to it to avoid schema design.

items.name: MuleSoft for Legacy Integration
items.description: Connectivity to legacy estate systems, such as mainframe policy administration and older claims platforms, is implemented through MuleSoft, which encapsulates legacy protocols and data formats behind reusable APIs. New direct couplings to legacy interfaces outside MuleSoft require an exception.

items.name: Multi-Cloud by Exception Only
items.description: Architectures spanning both clouds, or introducing any additional provider, require an explicit Architecture Review Board exception supported by a business case covering the added operational, security, and skills cost. Vendor-imposed hosting, such as a SaaS product running on a particular cloud, is recorded but does not constitute approval for custom multi-cloud builds.

items.name: No New TIBCO Implementations
items.description: No new integrations may be built on TIBCO; the existing estate is in run-down and is replaced opportunistically as connected systems are modernized. Any change to a TIBCO flow must first evaluate migrating that flow to MuleSoft, Service Bus, or Kafka.

items.name: PagerDuty for Alerting
items.description: Actionable alerts route through PagerDuty, where on-call schedules, escalation policies, and acknowledgment tracking are maintained per service. Alert definitions must map to runbook entries so responders know the expected action when paged.

items.name: PostgreSQL and SQL Server for OLTP
items.description: Transactional applications, including policy, billing, and claims services, use PostgreSQL or SQL Server as their system of record. The choice between them follows the application's ecosystem and licensing posture, and both are consumed as managed cloud services rather than self-hosted installs where possible.

items.name: RabbitMQ Deprecated
items.description: RabbitMQ is deprecated for new use, and existing brokers may continue only under a managed migration plan with a target decommission date. Enhancements to RabbitMQ-based integrations should be redirected to the approved platforms wherever feasible.

items.name: Redis for Caching
items.description: Redis is the standard technology for application caching, session state, and similar low-latency lookup needs. It is treated as ephemeral by design, and authoritative data must never reside solely in the cache.

items.name: Snowflake and Databricks for Analytics
items.description: Analytical and data science workloads run on Snowflake or Databricks, which host the governed warehouse and lakehouse layers respectively. Building analytics directly against OLTP databases or standing up alternative warehouse engines requires an architecture exception.

items.name: SonarQube for Quality Gates
items.description: Every pipeline executes SonarQube analysis, and builds must pass the enterprise quality gate covering code coverage, maintainability, and security hotspots before promotion. Gate thresholds are set centrally, and waivers are time-boxed and tracked.

items.name: Splunk for Logs
items.description: Application and infrastructure logs are centralized in Splunk with the standard retention, indexing, and access controls, supporting both operational troubleshooting and the audit retention obligations of a regulated insurer. Logs must follow the structured logging standard and exclude unmasked policyholder PII.

items.name: Callback Verification for Bank Account Changes
items.description: Requests to add or change vendor, claimant, or reinsurer bank account details are never actioned from email alone. Treasury staff verify each change by calling a known contact at an independently confirmed phone number on file, documenting the call before the new instructions take effect. This control is the carrier's primary defense against business email compromise schemes targeting claim and premium disbursements.

items.name: Dual Approval for Payments Over $10K
items.description: Any disbursement exceeding $10,000, whether check, ACH, or wire, requires two independent approvers within the payment system before release. The preparer may not also approve, and approver lists are reviewed quarterly against the delegation-of-authority matrix to confirm limits remain current.

items.name: Dunning Letters per Schedule
items.description: Past-due accounts receive standardized dunning correspondence on a fixed escalation schedule, with templates and timing approved by Legal and Compliance. For policyholder premium balances, the schedule is coordinated with state-mandated cancellation notice requirements so collection activity never conflicts with regulatory notice periods.

items.name: Invoice Approval Workflow
items.description: Every invoice is routed through the AP system's electronic approval workflow, with approvers determined by cost center and delegation-of-authority limits. Manual or out-of-system approvals are prohibited, and the workflow preserves a timestamped audit trail of who reviewed and approved each invoice before payment.

items.name: Payment Terms Enforced
items.description: Invoices are scheduled for payment according to the contracted vendor terms, neither paid early without Treasury approval nor allowed to slip past due. AP monitors on-time payment performance and captures early-payment discounts where the discount exceeds the carrier's short-term cost of funds.

items.name: Three-Way Match for PO Items
items.description: Invoices tied to purchase orders must match the PO and the goods-receipt or service-acceptance record on quantity and price before they can post. Mismatches outside tolerance are blocked automatically and routed to procurement and the requesting business unit for resolution rather than overridden by AP staff.

items.name: Weekly Aging Review
items.description: The receivables team reviews the full AR aging each week, covering premium receivables, agent and broker balances, and reinsurance recoverables. Balances crossing 30, 60, and 90 day buckets are flagged with a named owner and next action, and the summarized aging is circulated to the Controller for visibility into deteriorating accounts.

items.name: Write-Off Approval Matrix
items.description: Uncollectible balances may only be written off under a documented authority matrix that ties approval level to dollar amount, from receivables manager through Controller to CFO for the largest items. Each write-off requires evidence of collection effort, and aggregate write-off activity is reported quarterly to support bad-debt reserve adequacy.

items.name: 48-Hour Response to Auditor Requests
items.description: Routine auditor requests and follow-up questions receive a substantive response within two business days. Where the underlying support requires longer to assemble, such as actuarial reserve documentation or investment valuation detail, the owner communicates a committed delivery date within the same 48-hour window.

items.name: Annual Audit Plan Input
items.description: Finance leadership provides a formal risk assessment to internal audit during annual planning, identifying areas of elevated concern such as new accounting standards adoption, system conversions, or processes with recent control changes. This input is documented so the approved plan can be traced back to the risks the department raised.

items.name: Findings Tracked to Closure
items.description: Control deficiencies, adjustments, and management letter comments raised by the external auditors are logged with an accountable owner, remediation plan, and target date. Progress is reviewed with the Controller monthly and reported to the Audit Committee until each finding is verified closed, with prior-year items confirmed resolved before the next audit cycle begins.

items.name: Management Response Within 30 Days
items.description: When internal audit issues a draft report, the responsible finance manager delivers a written management response within 30 calendar days, either accepting the finding with a remediation plan and date or documenting a substantiated disagreement. Responses are reviewed by the Controller before submission to ensure commitments are realistic and properly resourced.

items.name: PBC List Tracked
items.description: The prepared-by-client request list from the external auditors is loaded into a shared tracker with an assigned owner and due date for every item. The audit liaison reviews status weekly during fieldwork, covering both GAAP and statutory audit requests, so late or stalled items are escalated before they threaten the audit timeline.

items.name: Remediation Tracked
items.description: Agreed remediation actions are entered into the issue-tracking system with owners and due dates, and status is reported at the department's monthly controls meeting. Items may only be closed once internal audit validates the corrective action, and overdue items are escalated to the CFO.

items.name: Annual Budget Calendar
items.description: FP&A publishes a budget calendar before the cycle opens, fixing the dates for assumption setting, business unit submissions, challenge sessions, and final approval. The calendar is sequenced so premium, loss, and expense planning across P&C, Life & Retirement, and group benefits align with actuarial plan-rate timelines and the Board's year-end approval meeting.

items.name: Executive Approval Required
items.description: The consolidated budget is presented to the executive committee for formal sign-off, and no business unit budget is considered final until that approval is recorded. Subsequent changes to the approved baseline require the same level of authorization, preserving the integrity of variance reporting throughout the year.

items.name: Monthly Forecast Update
items.description: The forecast is refreshed every month after the close, incorporating actual results, updated actuarial loss picks, and revised production outlooks from the business units. Each cycle follows a published submission deadline so the consolidated update reaches the CFO before month-end business reviews.

items.name: Rolling Four-Quarter Forecast
items.description: FP&A maintains a forecast that always extends four quarters ahead, crossing fiscal year boundaries rather than truncating at year end. The horizon covers premium production, loss ratios, investment income, and operating expenses by business segment, giving leadership a continuous forward view for capital and reinsurance planning.

items.name: Standardized Templates
items.description: All budget submissions use the templates issued by FP&A, with a common chart-of-accounts mapping, consistent expense allocation drivers, and prescribed assumption fields. This uniformity allows submissions from underwriting, claims, and corporate functions to be consolidated and compared without manual restatement.

items.name: Variance Explanation Required
items.description: Every forecast revision is accompanied by a written explanation of significant movements against both the prior forecast and the annual plan, attributing changes to specific drivers such as catastrophe activity, rate achievement, or expense timing. Unexplained variances above the materiality threshold are returned to the submitting unit before the forecast is accepted.

items.name: Aging of Reconciling Items
items.description: Open reconciling items are individually listed with the date they arose and an explanation, and items aging beyond 60 days are escalated to the assistant controller with a resolution plan. Items that cannot be substantiated within 90 days are assessed for write-off or adjustment rather than carried indefinitely.

items.name: Evidence Retained
items.description: Supporting documentation for each completed checklist task is attached or referenced within the close management tool and retained per the corporate records schedule. The evidence must be sufficient for an external auditor or examiner to reperform the task, including source reports, calculations, and approval trails.

items.name: JE Approval per Authority Matrix
items.description: Manual journal entries require approval by someone other than the preparer, with the required approval level escalating by entry size under the documented authority matrix. High-dollar and non-routine entries, such as reserve true-ups or impairments, route to the assistant controller or Controller, and the ledger system enforces these thresholds rather than relying on convention.

items.name: Materiality Thresholds
items.description: The Controller's office sets documented thresholds that scale reconciliation rigor to account risk and size, defining which accounts require full reperformance versus analytical review and what difference level must be investigated versus noted. Thresholds are reviewed annually and align with the materiality framework agreed with the external auditors.

items.name: Milestone Tracking
items.description: Key close milestones, including subledger close, reserve booking, and trial balance lock, are tracked in real time during each cycle with completion status visible to the whole close team. The close manager runs brief daily checkpoints during close week to confirm milestones are met or to reassign resources where they are at risk.

items.name: Monthly Balance Sheet Reconciliation
items.description: Every balance sheet account, including premium receivables, loss reserves, reinsurance balances, and investment holdings, is reconciled to its supporting subledger or external source each month. Reconciliations follow a standard format with preparer and reviewer sign-off, and completion status is monitored by the Controller's office against the close calendar.

items.name: No Backdating
items.description: Entries must be recorded in the period to which they relate while that period is open, and posting into closed periods is prohibited. Once a period is locked, corrections are made through current-period adjusting entries or, for material errors, through a formally approved reopening authorized by the Controller with full documentation of the reason.

items.name: Published Standard Close Calendar
items.description: The Controller's office publishes a close calendar for the full year, assigning a workday-numbered deadline to each activity from subledger cutoff through final consolidation. The calendar coordinates dependencies across actuarial reserve delivery, investment accounting feeds, and intercompany settlement so downstream tasks are never waiting on undefined inputs.

items.name: Required Sign-Offs
items.description: Every checklist task carries a preparer and a separate reviewer sign-off, captured electronically with name and timestamp. The close is not considered complete until all sign-offs are in place, and open items at period end must be formally dispositioned by the assistant controller rather than left blank.

items.name: Standardized Close Checklist
items.description: Each entity and ledger closes against a standardized checklist enumerating every required task, from accrual entries and reserve postings to intercompany eliminations and statutory-to-GAAP adjustments. The checklist is maintained centrally by the Controller's office, and additions or removals require its approval so coverage cannot quietly erode.

items.name: Supporting Documentation
items.description: Every manual entry is posted with attached support that explains the business purpose and substantiates the amounts, such as calculations, third-party statements, or actuarial memos. An approver who cannot understand and verify the entry from its attached support is required to reject it back to the preparer.

items.name: Variance to Schedule Reported
items.description: Tasks that miss their calendar deadline are logged with the cause and the recovery action taken, and a schedule-performance summary is included in the post-close review. Recurring slippage in the same activity triggers a root-cause assessment so the calendar or the underlying process is corrected rather than repeatedly missed.

items.name: Compensating Controls Documented
items.description: Where a duty conflict cannot reasonably be eliminated, a compensating control such as independent secondary review or detailed activity monitoring is designed, documented, and formally accepted by the Controller. Each accepted conflict and its compensating control is recorded in a register and reassessed during the annual SOX scoping exercise.

items.name: Conflicts Identified and Mitigated
items.description: User access across financial systems is analyzed against the matrix on a recurring cycle, using automated rule sets where the system supports them. Detected conflicts are removed through role redesign or access changes wherever practical, with particular attention to small treasury and statutory accounting teams where headcount makes conflicts more likely.

items.name: Key Controls Documented
items.description: Each key control over financial reporting is documented in the SOX repository with its risk and assertion mapping, control owner, frequency, and evidence requirements, supported by current process narratives and flowcharts. Documentation is refreshed whenever processes or systems change, with an annual certification by control owners that descriptions remain accurate.

items.name: SOD Matrix Maintained
items.description: A segregation-of-duties matrix defines incompatible function combinations across the general ledger, accounts payable, treasury, and payroll systems, such as vendor creation paired with payment approval. The matrix is owned by the controls team and updated whenever roles, systems, or processes change, with a full review at least annually.

items.name: Testing Calendar
items.description: Management's control testing follows a published annual calendar that sequences design and operating effectiveness testing across the year and stages high-risk controls early enough to allow remediation and retesting before year end. The calendar is coordinated with internal audit and the external auditors to maximize reliance and avoid duplicate requests on control owners.

items.name: Timely Deficiency Remediation
items.description: Control deficiencies identified through testing are logged, rated for severity, and assigned a remediation owner and target date commensurate with risk. Remediation progress is reviewed monthly by the SOX program lead, retesting confirms the fix operated effectively, and open deficiencies are reported to the Disclosure Committee and Audit Committee each quarter.

items.name: All Reporting per US GAAP
items.description: Consolidated and segment financial statements are prepared in conformity with US GAAP, including the insurance-specific guidance governing premium recognition, deferred acquisition costs, loss reserves, and long-duration contract measurement under ASC 944. GAAP results are maintained distinctly from statutory results, with the differences between bases reconciled and understood.

items.name: Annual Statement Accuracy
items.description: The Annual Statement blank for each entity, including Schedule F reinsurance detail, Schedule P loss development, and the investment schedules, is subject to documented preparation and independent review before officer attestation. Cross-checks and validation against NAIC edits are completed prior to filing, and errors discovered after submission are corrected through prompt amendment with regulator notification.

items.name: Board Package Five Days Before Meeting
items.description: The complete financial section of the board package is distributed through the board portal no fewer than five business days before each meeting. The production timetable works backward from this deadline, and any late-breaking material developments after distribution, such as a major catastrophe loss estimate, are communicated through a formally approved supplement.

items.name: CFO Review Required
items.description: The CFO personally reviews and approves all financial content before it is released to directors, confirming accuracy, consistency with reported results, and appropriateness of forward-looking commentary. This review is the final quality gate, and no finance material reaches the board portal without it.

items.name: Documented Accounting Policies
items.description: Each significant accounting policy is maintained as a written policy memo stating the authoritative guidance, the company's elected position, and its application to the company's products and transactions. Technical accounting maintains the policy library, assesses new FASB pronouncements for impact, and documents adoption positions before effective dates.

items.name: Flash Report by Workday Three
items.description: A preliminary flash report is issued by the third workday after period end, giving leadership an early estimate of written and earned premium, incurred losses, and headline operating results by segment. The flash draws on preliminary subledger data and actuarial indications, with known open items disclosed so readers understand its provisional nature.

items.name: Full P&L by Workday Ten
items.description: The complete management profit and loss package, including segment results, loss and expense ratios, and investment income detail, is published by the tenth workday. This package reflects the final closed ledger and serves as the authoritative basis for monthly business reviews and forecast updates.

items.name: NAIC Compliance
items.description: Statutory financial statements are prepared in accordance with NAIC statutory accounting principles as codified in the Accounting Practices and Procedures Manual, with any permitted or prescribed practices of the domiciliary states separately identified and disclosed. The statutory accounting team monitors NAIC working group activity and implements changes to SSAPs and annual statement instructions by their effective dates.

items.name: Policy Changes Approved by CFO
items.description: Adoption of new standards, changes in accounting method, and revisions to significant estimates methodology require written CFO approval before implementation, supported by a technical memo analyzing the alternatives. Material changes are also reviewed with the external auditors and disclosed to the Audit Committee before they take effect in reported results.

items.name: Standardized Format
items.description: Board financial reporting follows an approved standing format covering consolidated results, segment performance for P&C, Life & Retirement, and group benefits, capital and RBC position, and investment portfolio summary. Format changes require CFO approval and are introduced with bridging context so directors can follow trends across periods.

items.name: State Statutory Filings per Schedule
items.description: A consolidated filing calendar tracks every statutory obligation for each insurance entity, including quarterly and annual statements, RBC reports, premium tax returns, and state-specific data calls across all licensed jurisdictions. Each filing has a named owner and internal deadline set ahead of the regulatory due date, with late or amended filings escalated to the Controller.

items.name: Variance Analysis Required
items.description: Management reporting includes written analysis of results against plan, forecast, and prior year, with material variances attributed to specific drivers such as catastrophe losses, prior-year reserve development, rate change, or expense timing. Commentary must explain causes and expected persistence, and FP&A returns submissions that simply restate the numbers.

items.name: Access provisioning is approved before grant
items.description: Every grant of access to a financially-significant application is authorized by an appropriate approver before the access is provisioned, so that only properly authorized users can transact.

items.name: Automated premium-to-GL posting is complete and accurate
items.description: Premium amounts calculated in the policy administration system post to the general ledger completely and accurately, so that recorded premium revenue is supported by an independent recalculation with no unexplained variance.

items.name: Backups succeed and restores are periodically tested
items.description: Backups of financially-significant systems succeed on schedule and restores are periodically tested, so that financial data can be recovered intact in the event of loss or corruption.

items.name: Changes are approved before promotion to production
items.description: Every change promoted to a financially-significant production system is formally approved before deployment, so that only authorized, reviewed changes affect the financial reporting environment.

items.name: Control-deficiency remediation is tracked to closure with owner and due date
items.description: Every open ICFR control-deficiency remediation item is tracked with an accountable owner, a priority, and a committed due date, and none are overdue, demonstrating deficiencies are driven to closure.

items.name: Developers cannot approve or deploy their own changes
items.description: No individual can both author and approve, or both author and deploy, a change to a financially-significant production system, enforcing segregation of duties across the change lifecycle.

items.name: Emergency changes follow retroactive governance
items.description: Every emergency change to a financially-significant system is logged, retroactively approved, and subject to a post-implementation review, so that expedited changes remain governed even when normal pre-approval is bypassed.

items.name: Financial records retention and legal holds are enforced
items.description: In-scope financial records are retained under an enforced retention policy that meets the statutory minimum, legal holds are applied where required, and no records are prematurely deleted, satisfying the §802 records-retention requirements.

items.name: Financially-relevant batch jobs are monitored and failures resolved
items.description: Financially-relevant batch jobs are monitored, their failures raise alerts, and every failure is resolved, so that financial data is processed completely and accurately on schedule.

items.name: ICFR control matrix is complete and key controls are tested
items.description: The ICFR control matrix is complete with a named owner for every key control, all key controls are tested within the assessment cycle, and identified deficiencies are remediated, supporting management's §404 assessment of internal control over financial reporting.

items.name: Periodic user access recertification
items.description: Application owners review and formally recertify all user access to financially-significant systems each quarter so that access remains commensurate with current job responsibilities.

items.name: Privileged access is logged and independently reviewed
items.description: All privileged accounts on financially-significant systems are inventoried, their actions are captured in the SIEM, and each account is independently reviewed each quarter so that elevated access cannot be misused without detection.

items.name: Quarterly sub-certifications support the §302 certification
items.description: All required sub-certifiers complete and sign their quarterly sub-certifications on time, providing the documented basis on which the CEO and CFO rely to make the §302 disclosure certification.

items.name: Segregation of duties enforced on financial roles
items.description: Conflicting financial duties are prevented or mitigated by enforcing a segregation-of-duties ruleset across role assignments so that no single user can both initiate and conceal an erroneous or fraudulent transaction.

items.name: System interfaces reconcile on control totals
items.description: Data transmitted across in-scope system interfaces is reconciled on record counts and control totals between the sending and receiving systems, so that no financially-significant records are lost, duplicated, or altered in transit.

items.name: Timely deprovisioning of terminated users
items.description: Access for terminated personnel is revoked from financially-significant systems within the defined service-level agreement so that no former employee retains the ability to transact.

items.name: Effective Tax Rate Forecast
items.description: The tax department maintains a forecast of the annual effective tax rate, updated quarterly for changes in projected pre-tax income mix, tax-exempt investment income, and discrete items. Material movements in the forecast rate are explained to the CFO and incorporated into the financial forecast so earnings guidance reflects a current tax view.

items.name: Extension Requests as Needed
items.description: Where a return cannot be completed by its original due date, an extension is filed before the deadline under a documented decision by the tax director, accompanied by a payment of the estimated liability to avoid underpayment exposure. Extensions are treated as planned exceptions and tracked to ensure the extended return is filed well within the extension period.

items.name: Filing Calendar Maintained
items.description: The tax department maintains a master calendar of every recurring obligation, spanning federal and state income tax returns, premium tax filings in each licensed state, guaranty fund assessments, and information returns. Each item carries an owner, statutory due date, and internal preparation deadline, and the calendar is reconciled annually against the company's licensing footprint to catch new obligations.

items.name: Payment Deadlines Met
items.description: Estimated tax payments, premium tax remittances, and balances due are scheduled in advance with Treasury so funds are positioned and disbursed by each statutory deadline. Payment confirmations are retained, and any penalty or interest notice triggers a root-cause review and abatement request where grounds exist.

items.name: Quarterly Provision per ASC 740
items.description: The income tax provision is prepared each quarter in accordance with ASC 740, applying the estimated annual effective rate method and measuring deferred taxes on temporary differences, including insurance-specific items such as loss reserve discounting and unearned premium adjustments under the tax code. The provision workpapers follow a standard package reviewed by the tax director before results are released to financial reporting.

items.name: Uncertain Tax Positions Documented
items.description: Tax positions that may not be sustained on examination are identified, evaluated under the more-likely-than-not recognition and measurement framework, and documented in position memos with supporting technical analysis. The uncertain tax position inventory is reassessed each quarter for changes in law, audit activity, and statute expirations, with conclusions reviewed by the external auditors.

items.name: 13-Week Cash Forecast
items.description: A rolling 13-week forecast projects receipts and disbursements weekly, incorporating premium collection patterns, expected claim payment levels, reinsurance settlements, and scheduled items such as tax payments and dividends. The forecast is refreshed weekly, and forecast-to-actual variances are analyzed to keep projection accuracy improving over time.

items.name: Authorized Signers Current
items.description: Signer authority on every account is kept aligned with current employment and role, with departures and transfers triggering removal from bank records within days, not quarters. A periodic review compares bank-confirmed signer lists to the HR roster and the delegation-of-authority matrix, with discrepancies corrected and reported to the Treasurer.

items.name: Bank Account Inventory
items.description: Treasury maintains a complete register of every bank account held by any company entity, recording the institution, purpose, legal owner, signers, and linked services such as positive pay. New accounts may only be opened through Treasury under documented approval, and the inventory is confirmed against bank records at least annually.

items.name: Counterparty Limits
items.description: Exposure to any single issuer, counterparty, or guarantor is capped by limits scaled to credit rating and instrument type, aggregating bond holdings, deposits, derivative exposure, and reinsurance collateral arrangements. Limit utilization is monitored as positions and ratings change, and additions that would breach a cap require pre-trade approval or are blocked.

items.name: Daily Cash Position
items.description: Treasury prepares a consolidated cash position every business morning, capturing prior-day balances and current-day expected flows across operating, claims, and premium accounts. The position drives same-day decisions on funding disbursement accounts, concentrating excess balances, and placing short-term investments.

items.name: Dormant Accounts Closed
items.description: Accounts with no business activity over a defined period are reviewed for closure, and those without a justified continuing purpose, such as a state deposit or trust requirement, are closed with residual balances swept to concentration accounts. Closures are documented in the inventory so the account population reflects only what the business actually uses.

items.name: Duration Limits
items.description: Portfolio duration is managed within approved bands set relative to the duration of the underlying liabilities, recognizing the long-tail profile of certain P&C reserves and the long-duration nature of life and annuity obligations. Asset-liability mismatch is measured at the segment level, and positioning outside the bands requires documented approval from the investment committee.

items.name: Investment Policy Compliance
items.description: All portfolio activity, whether managed internally or by external advisers, must conform to the board-approved investment policy statement covering permitted asset classes, credit quality minimums, and concentration rules, as well as applicable state insurance investment laws. Compliance is tested against holdings on a recurring cycle, and breaches, including passive breaches from downgrades, are escalated and cured within defined timeframes.

items.name: Minimum Liquidity Maintained
items.description: The company holds available liquidity at or above a board-approved floor sized to cover stressed outflows, including elevated catastrophe claim payments, without forced sales from the investment portfolio. Treasury monitors headroom against the floor continuously and escalates to the CFO when projections show the buffer compressing, with committed credit facilities counted per the liquidity policy's eligibility rules.

items.name: Quarterly Investment Reporting
items.description: Treasury delivers a quarterly report to the investment committee and Board covering portfolio composition, book and market values, investment income, realized and unrealized gains and losses, impairment activity, and policy compliance status. The report also summarizes external manager performance against benchmarks and any policy exceptions granted during the period.

items.name: Annual Enrollment
items.description: An annual open enrollment window is planned, communicated, and executed on a published calendar, with plan changes, rates, and decision-support tools available to all eligible employees before the window opens. Elections are confirmed back to employees and reconciled to carrier and payroll systems before the new plan year takes effect.

items.name: Communications
items.description: Benefits communications, including summary plan descriptions, required notices, and enrollment guides, are issued on schedule and written in plain language. Employees receive timely notification of plan changes, deadlines, and where to get help, with delivery tracked for required disclosures.

items.name: FMLA and ADA Compliance
items.description: Leave requests are evaluated against Family and Medical Leave Act entitlements and Americans with Disabilities Act accommodation obligations, including the interactive process where applicable. Eligibility determinations, designations, and required notices are issued within statutory timeframes and retained as evidence of compliance.

items.name: Leave Tracking
items.description: All continuous and intermittent leave usage is recorded in a central system of record, with balances reconciled against entitlements and concurrent leave types coordinated correctly. Managers and payroll receive accurate, current leave status without exposing protected medical information.

items.name: Life Event Processing
items.description: Qualifying life events such as marriage, birth, divorce, or loss of other coverage are processed within the regulatory election window, with supporting documentation collected and verified. Mid-year changes flow through to carriers and payroll deductions without gaps or retroactive errors in coverage.

items.name: Return-to-Work Process
items.description: Each leave concludes with a structured return-to-work step covering fitness-for-duty certification where required, restoration to an equivalent position, and any transitional accommodations. Reinstatement dates are coordinated with the manager, payroll, and benefits so the employee returns without administrative disruption.

items.name: Vendor Management
items.description: Benefits carriers, brokers, and third-party administrators are managed under defined service-level agreements, with eligibility files monitored for transmission errors and periodic performance and billing reviews. Vendor issues affecting employee coverage are escalated and tracked to resolution.

items.name: Approval Process
items.description: Bonus pools and individual awards pass through a defined approval chain, with finance sign-off on funding and HR review for consistency and pay-equity impact before release. Awards above defined thresholds require senior leadership or committee approval.

items.name: Calculation Methodology
items.description: The formula linking company results, business-unit performance, and individual ratings to the bonus amount is written down before the performance period begins. Calculations are reproducible from source data, and any discretionary adjustments are recorded with rationale.

items.name: Eligibility Criteria
items.description: Each bonus plan documents who participates, including employment status, hire-date proration, leave treatment, and the effect of transfers or terminations before payout. Eligibility rules are applied uniformly and exceptions require documented approval.

items.name: Equity Analysis Performed
items.description: A periodic pay-equity analysis examines compensation across gender, race, and other protected characteristics for comparable roles, conducted under appropriate legal privilege where warranted. Identified disparities without legitimate explanation are remediated through a funded adjustment process.

items.name: Grant Process
items.description: Equity and long-term incentive grants are issued only under board- or committee-approved plans, with grant dates, award sizes, and participant lists documented and reconciled to the approving resolution. Award agreements are delivered to and acknowledged by each recipient.

items.name: Market Data Updated Annually
items.description: Salary structures are refreshed at least annually against reputable survey sources covering the insurance and broader financial services labor markets. Benchmark matches are reviewed for accuracy, and structure adjustments are approved and effective on a consistent cycle.

items.name: Pay Grades Defined
items.description: Every job is mapped to a documented pay grade with a defined salary range, based on job evaluation of skills, scope, and market value. Grade assignments and range placement rules guide hiring offers, promotions, and merit increases, with out-of-range pay requiring documented justification.

items.name: Payout Schedule
items.description: Payout timing is published in advance and adhered to, with awards processed through payroll in the designated cycle and correct tax withholding applied. Off-cycle or accelerated payouts follow a documented exception path.

items.name: Tax Implications Communicated
items.description: Participants receive plain-language guidance on the tax treatment of their awards at grant, vesting, and settlement, including withholding mechanics and key elections. Communications direct employees to personal tax advice rather than substituting for it, and withholding events are coordinated with payroll.

items.name: Vesting Schedules
items.description: Vesting terms for each award type are recorded in the administration system at grant and tracked through cliffs, installments, and any performance conditions. Terminations, leaves, and retirements are applied to vesting per plan rules, and upcoming vesting events are reconciled before settlement.

items.name: Access Controls
items.description: Access to employee records is limited to individuals with a documented business need, enforced through role-based permissions in HR systems and physical safeguards for paper files. Access rights are reviewed periodically and disclosures outside HR are logged.

items.name: EEO Reporting
items.description: Workforce demographic data is collected through compliant voluntary self-identification and submitted accurately in required EEO-1 and related government filings by their deadlines. Underlying data quality is validated before each submission cycle.

items.name: I-9 Compliance
items.description: Employment eligibility verification is completed for every new hire within the federally mandated timeframe, with Form I-9 sections executed correctly and reverifications tracked for expiring work authorizations. I-9 records are stored separately from personnel files and periodically self-audited.

items.name: Personnel Files Maintained
items.description: A complete personnel file is maintained for every employee, containing required employment documents, signed agreements, and performance records, with medical and investigation materials segregated into restricted files. File completeness is verified at hire and audited on a sampling basis.

items.name: Required Postings
items.description: Mandatory federal, state, and local employment notices are displayed in each work location and delivered electronically to remote employees. Postings are inventoried by jurisdiction and refreshed promptly when agencies revise them.

items.name: Retention Per Policy
items.description: Each record type carries a defined retention period reflecting federal, state, and insurance-regulatory requirements, and records are disposed of securely when the period lapses. Legal holds suspend destruction for records relevant to pending or anticipated litigation or regulatory inquiry.

items.name: Wage and Hour Compliance
items.description: Jobs are classified as exempt or non-exempt against FLSA and applicable state tests, with classifications reviewed when duties change. Time records, overtime, meal and rest breaks, and minimum wage requirements are administered correctly across every state in which the company employs staff.

items.name: Confidentiality Maintained
items.description: Information about complaints and investigations is shared strictly on a need-to-know basis, with participants instructed on discretion and case records held under restricted access. Anti-retaliation expectations are communicated to all parties and monitored after the case closes.

items.name: Documentation Standards
items.description: Investigators maintain a complete case file containing the complaint, interview notes, evidence collected, the analysis supporting each finding, and the outcome communicated. Documentation distinguishes fact from inference and is written with the expectation it may be reviewed by counsel or a regulator.

items.name: Employee Handbook Current
items.description: The employee handbook is reviewed on a set cycle and whenever law or company practice changes, with revisions vetted by legal counsel before publication. Jurisdiction-specific supplements are maintained for each state where the company employs staff, and superseded versions are archived.

items.name: Investigation Protocol
items.description: Every complaint is triaged promptly and assigned to a trained, conflict-free investigator who follows a defined sequence of planning, witness interviews, evidence review, and findings. Interim protective measures are considered at intake, and investigations conclude within target timeframes.

items.name: Policy Acknowledgments Tracked
items.description: Employees electronically acknowledge the handbook and designated critical policies at hire and upon each material revision. Acknowledgment completion is tracked centrally, non-responders are escalated to managers, and records are retained for use in disputes.

items.name: Updates Communicated
items.description: Policy changes are announced through defined channels with an effective date and a plain-language summary of what changed and why. Managers receive briefing material for changes affecting day-to-day supervision before the effective date.

items.name: Integration With Payroll and Benefits
items.description: Automated interfaces carry HRIS changes to payroll and benefits platforms on a defined schedule, with transmission errors and rejected records monitored and resolved before the next processing cycle. Integration mappings are documented and retested after any system change.

items.name: Regular Audits
items.description: Scheduled data-quality audits test critical fields such as job codes, reporting lines, compensation, and employment status against defined validation rules. Discrepancies are logged, root-caused, and corrected within target timeframes, with recurring error patterns driving process fixes.

items.name: Single Source of Truth
items.description: The HRIS is designated as the authoritative system for employee, position, and organizational data, and all downstream systems consume from it rather than maintaining parallel records. Data elements have named owners, defined formats, and controlled update paths.

items.name: Completion Rates Monitored
items.description: Training completion and pass rates are reported to department leaders on a regular cadence, with mandatory-training compliance tracked against target thresholds. Persistent shortfalls trigger root-cause review of content, scheduling, or accountability rather than repeated reminders alone.

items.name: Development Programs
items.description: Structured development offerings, including leadership curricula, stretch assignments, mentoring, and executive coaching, are matched to individual development plans for succession candidates and high-potentials. Program participation and progression outcomes are measured against the pipeline they are meant to fill.

items.name: High-Potential Identification
items.description: High-potential employees are identified through a calibrated assessment of performance and potential rather than single-manager nomination, with the pool reviewed for diversity and refreshed on a regular cycle. Identification criteria are documented and applied consistently across business units.

items.name: Mandatory Training Tracked
items.description: Required courses, including ethics, anti-fraud, information security, harassment prevention, and insurance regulatory topics, are assigned automatically based on role and jurisdiction with defined due dates. Completion is recorded in the learning management system and overdue assignments are escalated through management.

items.name: Role-Specific Curricula
items.description: Each job family carries a defined curriculum covering the technical and professional skills the role requires, from underwriting and claims proficiency to systems training. Curricula are reviewed with business leaders periodically and updated as processes, products, and tools change.

items.name: Succession Planning
items.description: Critical leadership and technical roles are identified annually, and each carries documented successors classified by readiness horizon. Succession plans are reviewed with executive leadership, and bench gaps trigger targeted development or external hiring strategies.

items.name: Access Termination Same Day
items.description: All system, application, building, and remote access is revoked no later than the employee's final working day, coordinated in advance between HR and IT. Involuntary separations trigger immediate revocation at notification, and a post-exit verification confirms no residual access remains.

items.name: Exit Checklist
items.description: Every separation runs against a standard checklist covering final pay, benefits continuation notices, asset recovery, system access, and outstanding obligations such as non-disclosure reminders. Checklist completion is verified and retained as the record that all separation steps occurred.

items.name: Exit Interview
items.description: Departing employees are offered a structured exit interview exploring reasons for leaving, management effectiveness, and workplace concerns. Responses are recorded confidentially, aggregated into attrition insights for leadership, and any compliance or conduct allegations raised are routed to employee relations.

items.name: Knowledge Transfer
items.description: Departing employees document in-flight work, key contacts, and critical know-how during the notice period, with the manager accountable for assigning each item a receiving owner. Transfer is prioritized for roles holding specialized expertise or single points of failure.

items.name: Access Provisioned
items.description: Network credentials, email, and the application entitlements defined for the role are provisioned through standard access-request workflows before the start date, following least-privilege principles. Day-one login is tested where possible so the employee is not idle waiting on access tickets.

items.name: Buddy Assigned
items.description: Each new hire is paired with a trained peer buddy outside the reporting line who answers everyday questions, makes introductions, and helps the employee navigate culture and unwritten norms. The buddy commits to regular contact through at least the first month.

items.name: Equipment Ready
items.description: Laptops, phones, peripherals, and any role-specific equipment are ordered upon offer acceptance, configured to standard images, and delivered to the work location or shipped to remote hires before day one. Readiness is confirmed in the pre-start checklist rather than assumed.

items.name: Manager Check-Ins Documented
items.description: Managers hold scheduled check-ins at least at each thirty-day milestone to review progress against the plan, surface obstacles, and adjust expectations. Notes from each check-in are recorded so the onboarding record shows feedback was given and acted upon.

items.name: Orientation Scheduled
items.description: New hires are enrolled in a scheduled orientation covering the company's businesses, values, compliance essentials, benefits enrollment, and key systems, beginning in the first week. Attendance is tracked and missed sessions are rescheduled rather than waived.

items.name: Probation Review
items.description: A formal review at the end of the introductory period documents whether the employee met the plan's expectations and results in a clear outcome of confirmation, extension with defined conditions, or separation. Adverse outcomes require HR consultation and documented supporting evidence.

items.name: Role-Specific Onboarding Plan
items.description: Each new hire receives a written plan defining the learning objectives, relationships to build, and deliverables expected at thirty, sixty, and ninety days, tailored to the specific role and business unit. The plan is prepared by the hiring manager before the start date and reviewed with the employee in week one.

items.name: Aligned to Company Objectives
items.description: Individual goals cascade from enterprise and business-unit objectives, and each goal identifies the higher-level priority it supports. Alignment is checked during goal review so effort across departments aggregates toward the company's strategic and transformation agenda.

items.name: Calibration Sessions
items.description: Before ratings are finalized, leaders meet in facilitated calibration sessions to compare proposed ratings across teams against common standards and the evidence behind them. Adjustments made in calibration are documented, and HR facilitates to guard against bias and rating inflation.

items.name: Documented in System by Q1
items.description: Finalized goals are entered into the performance management system no later than the end of the first quarter, creating the official record against which the year is assessed. Completion is monitored centrally and managers with unentered teams are escalated.

items.name: Feedback Documented
items.description: Review conversations are captured in the performance system, including ratings, narrative feedback, employee comments, and agreed development actions. The written record is specific enough to support subsequent compensation, promotion, or corrective-action decisions.

items.name: HR Involved
items.description: No formal improvement plan is initiated, extended, or concluded without HR review, ensuring the underlying concerns are performance-based, the documentation supports the action, and treatment is consistent with comparable cases. HR also screens for risk factors such as recent protected activity or accommodation requests.

items.name: Mid-Year and Annual Reviews
items.description: Every employee receives a documented mid-year progress review and a formal annual evaluation against their stated goals and the company's competency expectations. The mid-year checkpoint surfaces course corrections early enough to change the year-end outcome.

items.name: PIP Process Documented
items.description: Formal performance improvement plans follow a standard template stating the specific performance gaps, the measurable expectations to be met, the support provided, and the consequences of not meeting them. Plans are issued in writing and acknowledged by the employee.

items.name: SMART Goals
items.description: Each employee's goals are written to be specific, measurable, achievable, relevant, and time-bound, with success criteria defined up front rather than judged retrospectively. Managers review goal quality and return vague or unmeasurable goals for revision.

items.name: Timeline and Outcomes Tracked
items.description: Each plan carries a defined duration with scheduled progress reviews, and the result, whether successful completion, extension, or separation, is recorded with supporting evidence. Aggregate PIP outcomes are reviewed periodically for fairness and patterns across managers and demographics.

items.name: Approved Job Requisition Before Posting
items.description: No position is posted or sourced until a requisition with a current job description has been approved through the headcount governance chain, confirming budget and organizational need. Backfills and new positions follow the same control, and unapproved postings are removed.

items.name: Background Check Complete
items.description: Offers are contingent on satisfactory completion of background screening appropriate to the role, including criminal history, employment and education verification, and the financial-industry checks applicable to an insurance employer. Adverse findings are adjudicated through a documented individualized assessment compliant with FCRA and state law before any offer is rescinded.

items.name: Compensation Range Validated
items.description: Before posting, the compensation team confirms the role's grade and salary range against the structure and current market data, and the validated range is what appears in postings where pay transparency laws require disclosure. Recruiters negotiate only within the validated range absent documented exception approval.

items.name: Diverse Candidate Slate
items.description: Recruiters build candidate slates that include qualified candidates from underrepresented groups before interviews conclude, with slate composition tracked at the aggregate level. Searches that cannot produce a diverse slate document the sourcing effort undertaken and the constraint encountered.

items.name: Employee Referral Program
items.description: A formal referral program lets employees submit candidates through a tracked process, with defined award amounts, eligibility rules, and payout conditions tied to the referred hire's start and retention. Referrals enter the same structured assessment as all other candidates.

items.name: Hiring Committee for Senior Roles
items.description: Hires at or above designated senior levels require review by a hiring committee that examines the full candidate slate, interview evidence, and proposed terms before an offer is authorized. The committee check guards against single-stakeholder decisions on roles with outsized organizational impact.

items.name: Hiring Manager Intake
items.description: Each search opens with an intake meeting between recruiter and hiring manager that defines must-have qualifications, assessment criteria, the interview team, sourcing strategy, and a target timeline. The agreed profile becomes the reference point for screening and scorecards throughout the search.

items.name: Multiple Channels
items.description: Each search uses a mix of sourcing channels, such as job boards, direct outreach, professional and industry associations, campus pipelines, and internal mobility postings, rather than relying on a single source. Channel effectiveness is measured by hires and quality, informing future sourcing strategy.

items.name: Offer Approval Workflow
items.description: Every offer is routed through a defined approval chain validating the compensation package against the approved requisition, pay range, and budget before extension. Offers outside standard parameters, including sign-on awards or above-range salaries, require elevated approval, and only authorized parties extend formal offers.

items.name: Standardized Scorecards
items.description: Every interviewer submits a scorecard rating the candidate against the role's defined criteria on a common scale, with written evidence supporting each rating, before discussing the candidate with others. Scorecards are retained as the documented basis for selection decisions.

items.name: Start Date Coordination
items.description: Accepted offers trigger coordinated scheduling of the start date across the candidate, hiring manager, onboarding, IT provisioning, and payroll so the first day aligns with orientation cohorts and system readiness. Date changes are communicated promptly to every dependent party.

items.name: Structured Interviews
items.description: Interviews follow a planned structure in which each interviewer covers assigned competencies using prepared, job-related questions asked consistently of every candidate. Interviewers complete training on lawful, effective interviewing before participating in hiring decisions.

items.name: Base Images from Approved Registry Only
items.description: Container builds may pull base images only from the enterprise-approved registry, where images are curated, signed, and maintained by the platform team. Direct pulls from public registries into build pipelines or clusters are blocked at the network and admission-controller level.

items.name: Critical/High Findings Block Deployment
items.description: Any unresolved critical or high-severity SAST finding prevents the build from being deployed to production. Suppressions require a documented justification and follow the security exception process, with the finding tracked to remediation.

items.name: Input Validation
items.description: All API request payloads, parameters, and headers are validated against a defined schema before processing, with strict type, length, and range checks. Requests that fail validation are rejected with generic errors so internal structure is not disclosed, protecting downstream policy administration and claims systems from injection.

items.name: Mandatory Image Scanning
items.description: Every image is scanned for vulnerabilities and misconfigurations in the CI pipeline and again in the registry on a recurring schedule.
