Images with unremediated critical findings cannot be promoted, and running workloads are flagged when new vulnerabilities are disclosed against their layers.

items.name: Mandatory OWASP Top 10 Coverage
items.description: Scan profiles must demonstrably cover the current OWASP Top 10 categories, including injection, broken access control, and security misconfiguration. Coverage gaps in the tooling are documented and compensated with targeted manual testing.

items.name: No Critical CVEs in Production
items.description: Components with unpatched critical CVEs may not run in production. When a critical CVE is disclosed against a deployed dependency, the owning team must upgrade, patch, or apply a documented compensating control within the remediation SLA, or take the exposure through the exception process.

items.name: No Root Containers
items.description: Containers must run as a non-root user, with admission policies rejecting workloads that request UID 0, privileged mode, or host-level capabilities. This limits the blast radius if an application processing policyholder data is compromised at runtime.

items.name: No Secrets in Code
items.description: Passwords, API keys, certificates, and connection strings must never be committed to source control, embedded in container images, or stored in plaintext configuration. Automated secret-detection scanning runs on repositories and pipelines, and any detected secret is treated as compromised and rotated immediately.

items.name: No Sensitive Data in URLs
items.description: Policy numbers, SSNs, claim identifiers, tokens, and any other sensitive or personal data must never appear in URL paths or query strings, where they would persist in proxy logs, browser history, and referrer headers. Such values are carried only in request bodies or headers over TLS.

items.name: OAuth 2.0/OIDC for API Authentication
items.description: Every API must authenticate callers using OAuth 2.0 flows with OpenID Connect for identity assertion; API keys alone, basic auth, or home-grown token schemes are not acceptable. Tokens are scoped to the minimum claims required, short-lived, and validated on every request at the gateway and the service.

items.name: Pre-Production DAST Scans
items.description: Dynamic application security testing is executed against a running instance of the application in a pre-production environment before each production release. Authenticated scans are required for portals handling policyholder, agent, or claims data, and unresolved high-severity findings block the release.

items.name: Rate Limiting
items.description: APIs enforce per-client and per-endpoint rate limits at the gateway to blunt credential stuffing, quote-engine scraping, and denial-of-service attempts. Limits are tuned to legitimate business volumes (e.g., agent portal and partner integration traffic) and breaches generate security telemetry.

items.name: SAST Scan Required Before Merge
items.description: All code changes must pass a static analysis scan as a required check in the pull-request pipeline; merges are blocked until the scan completes. Scanner rulesets are centrally managed by Information Security and may not be weakened by individual teams.

items.name: Security Champion in Each Squad
items.description: Every delivery squad designates a trained security champion who acts as the first point of contact for security questions, triages findings, and represents the squad in the security community of practice. Champions receive ongoing training and are accountable for the squad's adherence to the gate requirements.

items.name: Security Gates at Design, Code, Test, and Deploy Phases
items.description: Each delivery phase carries a defined security gate: threat modeling and architecture review at design, static analysis and secure code review at code, dynamic and dependency testing at test, and configuration and deployment verification at release. A system cannot advance past a gate with unresolved blocking findings.

items.name: Use of Approved Vault Platforms
items.description: Applications retrieve secrets at runtime from an approved enterprise vault — HashiCorp Vault, Azure Key Vault, or AWS Secrets Manager — using workload identity rather than long-lived credentials. Vault access is least-privilege, audited, and secrets are rotated on a defined schedule.

items.name: Vulnerability Scanning of Third-Party Libraries
items.description: Software composition analysis runs in every build pipeline, inventorying all direct and transitive dependencies and matching them against known CVE data. Each application maintains a current software bill of materials so newly disclosed vulnerabilities can be traced to affected systems quickly.

items.name: All Security Risks Documented in Enterprise Risk Register
items.description: Every identified security risk — from audit findings, assessments, incidents, or exceptions — is recorded in the enterprise risk register with an owner, inherent and residual ratings, and a treatment plan. Security risks use the same taxonomy and scoring scales as other enterprise risks so they can be aggregated and compared.

items.name: Annual Control Attestation
items.description: Control owners formally attest each year that their controls are operating as designed, supported by evidence rather than assertion alone. Failed or partially effective controls generate findings that feed the risk register and remediation tracking.

items.name: Annual Reassessment of Critical Vendors
items.description: Vendors classified as critical — including those processing policyholder data or supporting core insurance operations — are reassessed at least annually. Reassessment validates that the vendor's posture has not degraded, reviews incidents and subcontractor changes, and refreshes the risk rating used in vendor governance.

items.name: NIST CSF or ISO 27001 Controls Mapped to Systems
items.description: Security controls are organized against NIST CSF or ISO 27001 and mapped to the in-scope systems and platforms each control protects. The matrix identifies the control owner, implementation status, and evidence source for every system, and is updated as systems are onboarded or retired.

items.name: Pre-Engagement Vendor Assessment
items.description: No third party may receive company data or system access until it has completed a security assessment proportionate to the sensitivity of the engagement, covering its security program, data handling, and incident obligations. Assessment results inform contract security terms and any conditions of approval.

items.name: Quarterly Review
items.description: The security portion of the register is formally reviewed each quarter to reassess ratings, confirm treatment progress, and retire closed items. Material changes and overdue treatments are escalated to the CISO and reported through enterprise risk governance.

items.name: Security Exception Process
items.description: Establishes a single governed path for deviating from any security standard: every exception must carry a formal risk acceptance by the accountable business owner, documented compensating controls that reduce the residual exposure, and explicit CISO approval, with a defined expiry and re-review date so exceptions cannot become permanent.

items.name: Data Minimization Principle Applied
items.description: Collection points, integrations, and reports are designed to capture and propagate only the fields required for their function. Periodic reviews of forms, feeds, and data warehouses identify and remove fields accumulating without a business justification.

items.name: Encryption, Masking, or Tokenization Required
items.description: Each documented PII or PHI field must be protected by at least one approved technique, with encryption for storage and transit, masking for display and non-production use, or tokenization for high-value identifiers, chosen according to the field's classification and use. Storing such fields in plaintext, including in logs and extracts, is a standards violation subject to remediation tracking.

items.name: Enforced Labeling
items.description: Classification labels are applied through tooling such as document tagging, database metadata, and email sensitivity marks, and downstream controls including DLP, sharing restrictions, and encryption policies act on the label automatically. Labels travel with the data so a Restricted claims file retains its protections when exported or attached.

items.name: Enforced Retention Policies
items.description: Approved retention schedules covering policy, claims, underwriting, and corporate records are implemented as automated controls in the systems and archives that hold the data, with disposal executed and logged when periods expire. Legal hold is the only mechanism that suspends disposal, and holds are tracked to release.

items.name: Four-Tier Classification of All Data
items.description: All data is classified as Public, Internal, Confidential, or Restricted at creation or ingestion, with data owners accountable for the assignment. Policyholder PII, claims medical evidence, and payment data fall in the upper tiers, and unclassified data defaults to Confidential treatment until assessed.

items.name: No Unnecessary PII
items.description: Personally identifiable information may not be held, copied, or replicated where the use case can be met with anonymized, aggregated, or pseudonymous data, a rule applied with particular force to analytics extracts, reporting marts, and vendor data shares. Discovery scans flag PII appearing outside sanctioned locations for remediation.

items.name: PII/PHI Fields Identified and Documented
items.description: Every system's data model is scanned and reviewed to identify fields containing PII or PHI, including names, SSNs, medical diagnoses, and treatment records embedded in claims notes and documents, and the findings are documented in the enterprise data inventory. The inventory is refreshed as schemas change so new sensitive fields cannot enter production undocumented.

items.name: Production Data Masked in Non-Prod Environments
items.description: Development, test, and training environments may not contain raw production data; refreshes pass through irreversible masking or synthetic-data generation that preserves referential integrity and realistic distributions for testing rating and claims logic. Exceptions require risk acceptance with compensating controls and a defined expiry.

items.name: Secure Data Transfer
items.description: Sensitive data leaving a system boundary, whether bordereaux to reinsurers, eligibility files to group-benefits clients, or medical records to TPAs, must move only over approved secure channels: SFTP, encrypted email, or a sanctioned managed file transfer service. Ad hoc methods such as unencrypted email attachments, consumer file-sharing sites, and removable media are prohibited, and DLP controls monitor for circumvention.

items.name: Tokenization for Payment Data
items.description: Card and bank account data used for premium collection and claims disbursement is replaced with tokens from an approved tokenization service, keeping primary account numbers out of carrier systems and shrinking PCI DSS scope. Detokenization is restricted to the payment processing boundary and is fully logged.

items.name: AES-256 for All Data at Rest
items.description: All persisted data, spanning databases, object storage, file shares, backups, and endpoint disks, is encrypted with AES-256 or a stronger approved algorithm. Platform-native encryption is acceptable when it meets the algorithm requirement and its keys are managed under the Key Management Standard.

items.name: Annual Certificate Rotation
items.description: Every certificate is rotated at least annually, with renewals tracked in a central certificate inventory and automated where the platform supports it. Expiry alerting begins well ahead of the rotation date so customer portals and B2B integrations with agencies and reinsurers do not fail on a lapsed certificate.

items.name: Database TDE for Sensitive Data Stores
items.description: Transparent Data Encryption is enabled on every database holding Confidential or Restricted data, including policy administration, claims, billing, and data warehouse platforms. TDE status is verified through configuration scanning, and any sensitive store found unencrypted is remediated as a tracked exception.

items.name: Enforced Rotation Policy
items.description: Keys and secrets rotate on defined schedules appropriate to their type and exposure, with automated rotation wherever the platform supports it and immediate out-of-cycle rotation upon suspected compromise or custodian departure. Rotation compliance is tracked centrally and overdue keys are escalated.

items.name: Keys Managed via Approved KMS/HSM
items.description: All cryptographic keys are generated and held within an approved key management service or hardware security module, with key custodian roles separated from the administrators of the systems the keys protect. Key usage is logged, and keys never leave the KMS or HSM boundary in plaintext.

items.name: Minimum 2048-Bit RSA Key Strength
items.description: Certificates issued or renewed for any ABC Insurance Group system must use RSA keys of 2048 bits or greater, or an approved equivalent-strength algorithm. Weaker certificates discovered in inventory scans, including on legacy policy-administration interfaces and vendor-managed endpoints, are scheduled for replacement.

items.name: No Hardcoded Secrets
items.description: Credentials, API keys, and cryptographic material may not be embedded in source code, configuration files, container images, or CI/CD pipeline definitions; applications retrieve secrets at runtime from an approved vault. Automated repository and image scanning detects hardcoded secrets, which are revoked and rotated on discovery, not merely deleted from the code.

items.name: TLS 1.2 Minimum for External Communications
items.description: Every external connection, including customer and agent portals, public APIs, vendor integrations, and reinsurer data exchanges, must negotiate TLS 1.2 or higher with approved cipher suites. Legacy protocols such as SSLv3, TLS 1.0, and TLS 1.1 are disabled at the endpoint, and partner connections that cannot meet the floor require a risk-accepted exception with a remediation date.

items.name: TLS 1.3 Preferred
items.description: New services are built to negotiate TLS 1.3 by default, and existing endpoints adopt it as platforms and partners allow. The newer protocol's forward secrecy and reduced handshake exposure make it the target state, with TLS 1.2 retained only for compatibility.

items.name: Access Requests Processed Within 4 Business Hours
items.description: Submitted access requests receive an approval decision from the entitlement owner or delegate within four business hours. Requests route automatically to the correct approver based on the system and role requested, and aging requests escalate so onboarding adjusters and seasonal claims staff are not left idle awaiting a decision.

items.name: All Privileged Access via PAM Tool
items.description: Administrative access to servers, databases, network devices, and cloud consoles is brokered exclusively through the approved PAM platform, which vaults and rotates the underlying credentials. Direct use of shared or local admin accounts outside the tool is prohibited and monitored, including for vendors administering hosted insurance platforms.

items.name: Break-Glass Procedures
items.description: Documented emergency access procedures allow authorized staff to obtain elevated access during outages or incidents, such as restoring a down claims platform during a catastrophe event, but only with dual approval and a mandatory, tamper-evident audit trail of every action taken. Break-glass credentials are sealed, monitored for use, rotated after each invocation, and every use triggers a post-incident review.

items.name: Just-in-Time Access
items.description: Privileged entitlements are granted on demand for a defined task and time window rather than held permanently, with elevation requests approved and automatically revoked at expiry. This keeps standing privileged accounts near zero and shrinks the attack surface an intruder can harvest.

items.name: Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA)
items.description: Multi-factor authentication is mandatory for all external access including remote workforce, agent, and broker connections, for every privileged account, and for sensitive systems such as claims payment, policy administration, and HR platforms. Phishing-resistant factors are preferred, SMS-only fallback is restricted, and MFA enrollment is enforced at account creation so no in-scope account operates on a password alone.

items.name: Provisioning Within 24 Hours
items.description: Approved access is technically provisioned within 24 hours, through automated joiner-mover workflows where integration exists and tracked manual fulfillment elsewhere. Provisioning actions are logged against the originating request so every active entitlement traces to an approval, and SLA performance is reported to IAM governance.

items.name: Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)
items.description: All system access is granted through defined roles rather than individual entitlements, with each role documented as to its purpose, permissions, and owner, and with periodic access reviews certifying that assignments remain appropriate. Role design enforces least privilege and segregation of duties, for example separating claims adjudication from claims payment release, and review-identified excess access is revoked within defined timelines.

items.name: Service Account Management
items.description: Every service account is inventoried with a documented purpose and accountable owner, configured as non-interactive so humans cannot log in with it, scoped to least privilege for its specific integration or batch function, and subject to automated password or key rotation. Interactive use of a service account, common in legacy batch processing for policy and billing cycles, is detected and treated as a security event.

items.name: Session Recording for Admin Activities
items.description: Privileged sessions launched through the PAM platform are recorded, with keystroke or video capture retained per the retention schedule and protected from alteration by the administrators being recorded. Recordings support incident forensics and are sampled during periodic reviews of high-risk activity such as production database changes.

items.name: 15-Minute Escalation for Sev1 Incidents
items.description: Events classified Severity 1 trigger escalation to the incident commander and designated leadership within 15 minutes of classification, through an on-call rotation with automated paging and acknowledgment tracking. Failed acknowledgments escalate automatically up the chain so an active breach never waits on a single unreachable responder.

items.name: Annual Full IR Simulation
items.description: Once a year, a full-scope simulation exercises the response end to end, including technical containment actions, executive crisis management, and regulator and customer communication drafting, going beyond discussion to hands-on execution. The simulation tests the 72-hour notification workflow and produces a formal after-action report with plan updates.

items.name: Documented Forensic Tools and Procedures
items.description: Approved forensic tooling for disk, memory, log, and cloud-artifact acquisition is maintained in a ready state, and step-by-step procedures cover acquisition, chain of custody, and analysis. Designated responders are trained on the procedures, and engagement terms with an external forensics firm are pre-established for incidents exceeding internal capacity.

items.name: Documented IR Plan with Severity Definitions
items.description: A maintained incident response plan defines roles, communication paths, decision authority, and the severity classification scheme used to triage every event. The plan addresses insurance-specific scenarios such as claims-data exfiltration and ransomware against policy administration, aligns with breach-notification obligations including the 72-hour NYDFS and GDPR clocks, and is reviewed and updated at least annually.

items.name: Evidence Preservation Within 1 Hour
items.description: Once an incident is declared, preservation of volatile and at-risk evidence, including memory captures, relevant logs, and snapshots of affected systems, begins within one hour, before remediation actions can destroy it. Preserved evidence is stored with chain-of-custody documentation so it remains usable for regulatory proceedings and potential claims litigation.

items.name: Quarterly Tabletop Exercises
items.description: Each quarter, a facilitated tabletop walks responders and business stakeholders through a realistic scenario, rotating across threats such as ransomware in the claims environment, vendor compromise at a TPA, and insider data theft. Findings, gaps, and action items are documented and tracked to closure, and scenarios periodically include legal, communications, and the privacy office to rehearse notification decisions.

items.name: Severity Definitions
items.description: Establishes the enterprise severity scale for security events: Severity 1 for an active breach or data loss, Severity 2 for an attempted breach, Severity 3 for an identified vulnerability, and Severity 4 for an anomaly warranting investigation. Consistent application of these definitions drives escalation timing, executive notification, and regulatory-clock decisions, and triage staff are trained to classify against them rather than by judgment call.

items.name: Audit Logging Enabled
items.description: Database audit logging captures privileged operations, schema changes, authentication events, and access to sensitive tables such as policyholder PII and claims medical data. Logs ship to the central SIEM, are protected from modification by database administrators, and are retained per the records schedule to support investigations and regulatory examinations.

items.name: Automated Misconfiguration Detection
items.description: Misconfigurations such as public storage buckets, open security groups, and unencrypted volumes are detected automatically and routed to owning teams with severity-based remediation deadlines, and the highest-risk findings trigger auto-remediation or alerting in near real time. Findings involving stores of policyholder data are prioritized above the standard SLA.

items.name: CIS Benchmarks Applied
items.description: Every operating system image must be configured against the applicable Center for Internet Security (CIS) benchmark at the level designated for its environment tier. Deviations from benchmark recommendations require a documented justification and risk acceptance, and benchmark compliance scores are reported through the configuration management tooling.

items.name: CSPM Enabled
items.description: A cloud security posture management platform is deployed across all cloud accounts and subscriptions, continuously evaluating resources against the carrier's hardening baselines and benchmark frameworks. Coverage is verified as new accounts are created so shadow environments cannot escape monitoring.

items.name: DMZ Required
items.description: All internet-facing services, including customer portals, agent and broker gateways, and partner file-transfer endpoints, are deployed in a demilitarized zone separated from internal networks by inspected control points. Systems in the DMZ hold no persistent sensitive data and reach internal services only through tightly scoped, monitored connections.

items.name: Database TDE Enabled
items.description: Transparent Data Encryption is enabled on all database instances in scope, encrypting data files, transaction logs, and backups at the storage layer with keys managed under the Key Management Standard. Compliance is checked through automated configuration scans, and new instances cannot be promoted to production without TDE verified.

items.name: Documented Firewall Rules
items.description: Every firewall rule is documented with its business justification, owner, and review date, and rule changes flow through change management with security approval. Periodic recertification removes expired and shadowed rules so the rulebase reflects current data flows rather than accumulated history.

items.name: Microsegmentation for Sensitive Workloads
items.description: Workloads processing Restricted data, including claims payment, policy administration, and PII-bearing databases, are isolated with microsegmentation that permits only explicitly defined east-west flows between them. Segmentation policies follow the workload across data center and cloud placement and are validated through periodic traffic analysis and penetration testing.

items.name: Quarterly IAM Policy Reviews
items.description: Cloud IAM roles, policies, and trust relationships are reviewed each quarter to remove unused permissions, over-broad wildcard grants, and dormant identities, with particular attention to cross-account access used by vendors and managed-service providers. Review outcomes are documented and permission reductions are tracked to completion.

items.name: Restricted Network Access
items.description: Databases accept connections only from authorized application tiers and administrative jump hosts, enforced through firewall rules, security groups, and private network placement; no database listens on a public interface. Direct workstation-to-database connectivity is limited to approved administrators through controlled paths.

items.name: Secure Configuration Baseline
items.description: A version-controlled baseline defines the approved settings for each supported OS platform, and all production hosts are checked against it for drift. Changes to the baseline follow change management, and systems found out of compliance are remediated or formally excepted within defined timeframes.

items.name: Unnecessary Services Disabled
items.description: Builds must remove or disable any service, daemon, protocol, or default account not required for the system's documented business function, reducing the attack surface exposed to the network. Service inventories are reviewed when a system's role changes and during periodic configuration audits.

items.name: Assume Breach for All Network Access
items.description: All network access must be designed on the assumption that the environment is already compromised, so no connection is trusted simply because it originates inside the corporate network. Architectures favor segmentation, encrypted internal traffic, and continuous monitoring that limit lateral movement and blast radius when a breach occurs.

items.name: Data Flow & Trust Boundaries
items.description: Requires that every data flow between systems, networks, and external parties be documented with its trust boundary classifications, so the architecture team can see where data crosses from higher-trust to lower-trust zones. Maintained data flow diagrams identify the sources, destinations, transport mechanisms, and boundary crossings for sensitive data such as policyholder NPI, giving security reviews, threat models, and regulatory responses an authoritative picture of where controls must sit.

items.name: Defense in Depth Strategy
items.description: Requires multiple independent layers of security controls across the network, application, data, and endpoint tiers, so that the failure or bypass of any single control does not expose the carrier's systems or nonpublic information. Architects must demonstrate in design reviews that each critical asset is protected by overlapping controls, such as network segmentation and firewalls, application-level authentication and input validation, data encryption and access governance, and endpoint protection and hardening, rather than relying on a single perimeter.

items.name: Security Reference Architecture
items.description: Establishes standard, pre-approved security patterns for cloud deployments, covering constructs such as VPC design, subnet segmentation, and security group rules, as well as for on-premises and hybrid environments. Project teams build from these published reference patterns rather than designing security topology from scratch, which keeps controls consistent across the carrier's P&C, Life & Retirement, and group benefits platforms and shortens architecture review cycles.

items.name: Threat Modeling (STRIDE)
items.description: Requires every new system to complete a STRIDE threat modeling exercise, analyzing spoofing, tampering, repudiation, information disclosure, denial of service, and elevation of privilege threats, before its design can be approved. The resulting threat model documents identified threats, their mitigations, and accepted residual risks, and serves as a gate in the architecture review process so security weaknesses are addressed in design rather than discovered in production.

items.name: Verify Explicitly With Least Privilege
items.description: Every access request must be explicitly authenticated and authorized using all available signals, including user identity, device health, location, and the sensitivity of the requested resource, with access granted at the least privilege necessary and re-evaluated rather than persisting indefinitely. Designs incorporate the assume-breach posture throughout, applying just-in-time and just-enough access for administrative functions.

items.name: All Applications Log to the Enterprise SIEM
items.description: Every application, whether built in-house, purchased, or SaaS, must ship its security-relevant logs to the enterprise SIEM platform (Sentinel or Splunk). Onboarding to the SIEM is a go-live requirement, with log source, format, and parsing validated by the security operations team before production release.

items.name: Documented Playbooks for the Top 20 Security Alerts
items.description: Written response playbooks must exist for the 20 most frequent or highest-impact security alert types, each defining triage steps, investigation queries, containment actions, escalation criteria, and closure requirements. Playbooks are maintained in the SOC knowledge base and updated as detection content and the environment change.

items.name: False Positive Rate Below 10 Percent
items.description: The alerting program must maintain a false positive rate below 10 percent, measured from analyst triage dispositions. Detection rules that exceed the threshold are flagged for retuning or retirement, and the metric is reported as part of security operations performance reviews.

items.name: Log Retention
items.description: Establishes the tiered retention schedule for security logs across the enterprise: 90 days in hot storage for immediate search and active investigation, one year in warm storage for trend analysis and slower-burn investigations, and seven years in archive to satisfy compliance and regulatory obligations, including insurance-sector examination and audit-trail requirements. All log sources feeding the security tooling must conform to this schedule, and archived logs must remain retrievable for the full retention period.

items.name: Log Shipping Within Five Minutes
items.description: Security events must arrive in the SIEM within five minutes of generation, so detection rules and analyst investigations operate on near-real-time data. Log pipeline latency is monitored, and sources that fall behind the five-minute target generate operational alerts for remediation.

items.name: Quarterly Documented Threshold Tuning
items.description: Alert thresholds for each detection rule must be documented, including the rationale for the configured values, and reviewed and tuned at least quarterly. Tuning sessions incorporate recent incident findings, changes to the environment, and analyst feedback, and all threshold changes are recorded with approval and effective date.

items.name: Quarterly Playbook Testing
items.description: Each playbook must be exercised at least quarterly, through live alert handling, simulation, or tabletop walkthrough, to confirm the documented steps still work against current tooling and system configurations. Gaps identified during testing are remediated and the playbook revised with a record of the test date and outcome.

items.name: Security Event Logging
items.description: Defines the minimum set of security-relevant events that every system must capture: authentication attempts, authorization decisions, access to data, and configuration changes. Logging these categories consistently across applications and infrastructure gives the carrier the evidence needed to detect unauthorized activity against policyholder data, support incident investigations, and demonstrate control operation to auditors and regulators.

items.name: Annual Third-Party Penetration Test
items.description: An independent third-party firm must conduct a penetration test of the carrier's environment at least annually, with scope covering externally facing and key internal systems. Findings are risk-rated, tracked to remediation, and the engagement reports are retained as evidence for regulatory and audit requirements, including NYDFS testing expectations.

items.name: Critical and High Vulnerabilities Tracked to Closure
items.description: Every critical and high severity vulnerability must be recorded in the remediation tracking system with an assigned owner, target date aligned to the patching SLA, and current status, and remains open until the fix is verified by rescan or retest. Aging items are escalated through the vulnerability management governance process.

items.name: Exceptions Require CISO Approval
items.description: Any deviation from required remediation, whether a deferral, a compensating control in place of a fix, or formal risk acceptance, must be approved by the CISO. Approved exceptions are documented with justification, compensating measures, and an expiration date that forces re-review rather than permitting indefinite exposure.

items.name: Monthly Scans for Non-Production Systems
items.description: Non-production environments, including development, test, and staging systems, must be scanned at least monthly. The cadence recognizes their lower direct exposure while still catching vulnerable components before they promote to production and preventing non-prod from becoming an unmonitored foothold.

items.name: Patch Management SLA
items.description: Sets the maximum remediation timelines for applying security patches based on vulnerability severity: critical vulnerabilities within 72 hours, high within 7 days, medium within 30 days, and low within 90 days. The clock starts when the vulnerability is confirmed applicable to the carrier's environment, and SLA compliance is tracked and reported so unpatched exposure on systems handling policyholder data is bounded and visible to management.

items.name: Quarterly Internal Penetration Testing of Critical Systems
items.description: Systems classified as critical, such as policy administration, claims, and payment platforms, must undergo internal penetration testing each quarter, performed by the internal security testing team. The higher cadence ensures changes to these systems are probed for exploitable weaknesses well before the next external engagement.

items.name: Weekly Scans for All Production Systems
items.description: Every production system must be scanned for vulnerabilities at least weekly using authenticated scans wherever technically feasible, ensuring newly disclosed flaws in internet-facing and core insurance platforms are identified within days. Missed or failed scans are treated as coverage gaps and remediated promptly.

items.name: Approved Templates for Common Agreements
items.description: Legal publishes and owns standard templates for recurring agreement types, including NDAs, producer and agency agreements, vendor services agreements, statements of work, and data processing addenda. Templates embed ABC Insurance Group's required clauses on confidentiality, regulatory compliance, and audit rights, and only the current CLM-published version may be used.

items.name: Contract Lifecycle Management System Required
items.description: All contracts must be created, routed, executed, and stored through the enterprise CLM platform; side agreements held in email or shared drives are prohibited. The CLM record is the authoritative source for contract status, parties, value, and key dates used by Finance, Procurement, and Compliance reporting.

items.name: Deviation Requires Legal Approval
items.description: Any edit to template language beyond designated fill-in fields must be approved by a Legal attorney before the document is sent to a counterparty. Approved deviations are logged with rationale so frequently requested changes can be evaluated for incorporation into the next template revision.

items.name: Fully Executed Copies Retained
items.description: A complete, countersigned copy of every agreement, including all exhibits, schedules, and amendments, must be captured in the contract repository within 5 business days of execution. Paper originals for instruments requiring wet signatures, such as certain reinsurance and regulatory filings, are retained by Legal Operations with the repository record noting their physical location.

items.name: Legal Review of All Contracts Over $50K
items.description: Any agreement with total expected value above $50,000, and any contract involving policyholder data, reinsurance, or regulatory undertakings regardless of value, must be reviewed and cleared by a Legal attorney before signature. Business units may not split contracts to fall under the threshold, and the reviewing attorney is recorded in the CLM.

items.name: Obligation Monitoring
items.description: Material obligations such as service levels, insurance and security requirements, audit rights, and regulatory flow-down clauses are extracted into the CLM at onboarding and assigned to a named business owner. Owners attest to compliance status at least quarterly, and breaches by either party are escalated to Legal for cure-notice or remediation handling.

items.name: Redline Tracking
items.description: All negotiated changes must be exchanged as tracked revisions and stored as versioned documents in the CLM so the negotiation history is reconstructible. Final execution versions are compared against the last agreed redline to confirm no unapproved language was introduced.

items.name: Renewal Tracking
items.description: Every contract with a renewal or auto-renewal provision carries CLM-managed alerts beginning at least 90 days before the renewal or non-renewal notice deadline, with longer lead times for reinsurance treaties and core system vendors. The business owner must record an affirmative renew, renegotiate, or terminate decision before the notice window closes.

items.name: Signature Authority Matrix
items.description: A board-approved matrix defines which officers and delegates may execute agreements, tiered by contract value, duration, and risk class (e.g., reinsurance treaties, producer agreements, vendor contracts). Signatures outside the matrix are invalid and must be escalated to the General Counsel for ratification or rescission. The matrix is reviewed annually and updated within 30 days of any officer change.

items.name: Standard Playbook
items.description: Negotiations are conducted against a Legal-maintained playbook that specifies preferred, fallback, and walk-away positions for recurring clauses such as limitation of liability, indemnification, data protection, and insurance requirements. Positions outside the playbook require attorney sign-off, and the playbook is refreshed at least annually to reflect new regulatory and market conditions.

items.name: Termination and Expiration Management
items.description: Terminations follow a documented close-out checklist covering final payments, return or destruction of policyholder and company data, transition assistance, and survival-clause obligations. Expired and terminated contracts are marked closed in the CLM and retained per the records schedule rather than deleted.

items.name: Legal Review for Risk
items.description: Before an involuntary termination is communicated, Legal assesses risk factors including protected-class considerations, recent complaints or whistleblower activity, pending leave or accommodation requests, and documentation adequacy. High-risk separations require written Legal clearance and may be restructured or delayed pending remediation.

items.name: Non-Compete and NDA Requirements
items.description: Confidentiality agreements are required for all employees before access to company systems, and restrictive covenants such as non-competition and non-solicitation provisions are applied only to roles where they are justified and enforceable under the governing state's law. Legal maintains state-specific covenant language and reviews enforceability annually as statutes change.

items.name: Onboarding Compliance
items.description: New-hire onboarding must capture executed employment documents, I-9 verification, and any required insurance licensing or appointment paperwork before the employee begins regulated work. HR confirms completion in the HRIS, and missing items trigger escalation within the first week of employment.

items.name: Separation Agreement Templates
items.description: Where severance is offered, Legal-maintained separation agreement templates are used, incorporating jurisdiction-specific release requirements such as ADEA consideration and revocation periods. Template deviations and individually negotiated terms require attorney approval before presentation to the employee.

items.name: Standardized Offer Letters
items.description: All offers of employment use Legal-approved letter templates with role-appropriate variants for licensed producers, executives, and standard staff. Compensation terms, contingencies such as background checks and licensing verification, and at-will language may not be modified without Legal and HR approval.

items.name: Termination Checklist
items.description: Every separation follows a standard checklist covering final pay and benefits compliance, system and facility access revocation, recovery of company property, and termination of any state insurance appointments held by the departing employee. The completed checklist is retained in the personnel file.

items.name: Annual Filings on Time
items.description: Annual reports, franchise tax filings, and corporate registrations are tracked on a compliance calendar with owners and lead-time alerts, and no entity may lapse into delinquent status. Filing confirmations are stored with the entity record, and any notice of pending forfeiture is escalated to the General Counsel the day it is received.

items.name: Approved at Next Meeting
items.description: Minutes are presented for formal approval as the first order of business at the following meeting of the same body, with corrections captured in the approving meeting's record. Unapproved minutes are clearly marked as drafts and are not released to examiners or auditors without Corporate Secretary direction.

items.name: Current Entity Inventory
items.description: Legal maintains a complete register of all legal entities, including each insurer's domicile, licenses, NAIC company code, officers and directors, and ownership within the holding company structure. The inventory is reconciled quarterly against state records and the Schedule Y organizational chart, and changes such as formations, mergers, or dissolutions are recorded within 10 business days.

items.name: Draft Minutes Within Seven Days
items.description: The Corporate Secretary circulates draft minutes to the chair within seven calendar days of each meeting while discussion and dissents are fresh. Drafts record attendance, quorum, matters considered, resolutions adopted, and abstentions or recusals, at a level of detail consistent with privilege and litigation considerations.

items.name: General Counsel Review Required
items.description: The General Counsel or a designee reviews every packet before distribution for legal accuracy, privilege protection, disclosure consistency, and alignment with prior board actions. Items presenting material legal or regulatory exposure carry an explicit Legal assessment in the materials.

items.name: Materials Distributed Five Days in Advance
items.description: Complete board and committee packets must be posted to the secure board portal no later than five business days before the meeting. Late additions require Corporate Secretary approval and are flagged as supplemental, and chronic late submissions are reported to the committee chair.

items.name: Registered Agent Maintained
items.description: Every entity must have a current registered agent in each jurisdiction where it is formed or qualified to do business, so that service of process, regulatory notices, and policyholder suits are received and routed reliably. Agent appointments are verified annually and updated immediately upon any agent or address change.

items.name: Signed and Retained
items.description: Approved minutes are signed by the Corporate Secretary, entered into the official minute books, and retained permanently in accordance with corporate records requirements and state insurance examination expectations. Access to minute books is restricted and logged.

items.name: Standardized Format
items.description: All submissions follow the Corporate Secretary's templates, including an executive summary, requested action or resolution language, risk and regulatory implications, and supporting detail. Consistent structure lets directors compare items across meetings and supports an orderly minute-taking and resolution record.

items.name: Assignment Agreements
items.description: All employees sign invention assignment provisions at hire, and contractors and development vendors must execute work-for-hire or present assignment terms before development begins. Legal verifies the chain of title for each disclosure and cures any gaps with confirmatory assignments before filing or asserting rights.

items.name: Infringement Monitoring
items.description: Watch services and periodic marketplace reviews surface confusingly similar marks, domain names, and look-alike insurance offerings, which matter because imposter brands create direct consumer-harm and regulatory exposure for a carrier. Detected conflicts are assessed within 30 days and addressed through escalating responses from demand letters to opposition or litigation.

items.name: Invention Disclosure Process
items.description: Employees and contractors submit potentially protectable innovations through a standard disclosure form capturing the problem solved, technical approach, contributors, and any public exposure or third-party components. Legal acknowledges receipt, logs the disclosure in the IP register, and triages it for evaluation within 30 days.

items.name: Patentability Assessment
items.description: Disclosed inventions are assessed by IP counsel for novelty, subject-matter eligibility, and commercial value to the insurance business, with a documented decision to pursue patent protection, hold as a trade secret, or release. Time-sensitive items, such as inventions nearing public demonstration, are expedited to preserve filing rights.

items.name: Renewal Tracking
items.description: Registration maintenance deadlines, including declarations of use and renewal windows, are docketed with alerts at least six months in advance so no mark lapses unintentionally. Renewal decisions weigh continued commercial use, and abandonments are deliberate, documented choices approved by IP counsel.

items.name: Trademark Portfolio
items.description: Legal maintains a register of all house marks, product names, and logos, recording registration status, classes, and jurisdictions for each. New product or program names proposed by the business must be cleared through a trademark search and Legal approval before market use or filing.

items.name: Accruals
items.description: Outside counsel and vendor work performed but not yet invoiced is accrued monthly so legal expense lands in the correct accounting period, supporting accurate statutory and GAAP reporting. Firms must submit accrual estimates by the monthly deadline, and persistent non-compliance affects panel standing.

items.name: Budget Tracking
items.description: Legal operates an annual budget broken down by practice area and matter type, with actuals tracked monthly through the e-billing system. Variances above 10% at the practice-area level require a documented explanation and a reforecast submitted to Finance.

items.name: CLM, E-Billing, and Matter Management Systems
items.description: The department's core platforms, contract lifecycle management, electronic billing, and matter management, are the mandatory systems of record for contracts, invoices, and legal matters respectively. New legal tools must be procured through IT and Legal Operations governance, integrate with these core systems where applicable, and meet the carrier's information security standards for handling confidential and policyholder data.

items.name: Cost Reduction
items.description: Legal Operations maintains an active cost-reduction agenda including alternative fee arrangements, insourcing of repeatable work, use of staffing levels appropriate to matter complexity, and competitive bidding for significant matters. Savings initiatives carry quantified targets and are reported to the General Counsel semiannually.

items.name: Data Standards
items.description: Common reference data, including matter types, practice areas, entity names, and cost centers, follows controlled picklists aligned to Finance and enterprise data definitions. Required fields are enforced at intake so records are complete at creation, and data quality is sampled quarterly with correction assignments for owning teams.

items.name: Outside Counsel Spend Analysis
items.description: Spend is analyzed at least quarterly by firm, matter type, timekeeper level, and rate, benchmarking effective rates and matter costs against prior periods and market data. The analysis feeds rate negotiations, panel reviews, and decisions about which work to move to lower-cost firms or in-house staff.

items.name: Reporting
items.description: Standard dashboards covering matter volumes, cycle times, contract turnaround, and spend are produced from the core systems on a defined monthly and quarterly cadence for the General Counsel and business partners. Ad hoc reporting requests are fulfilled from system data, not manually maintained shadow trackers.

items.name: All Matters Logged in System
items.description: Every litigation, arbitration, regulatory enforcement, and significant pre-suit dispute is opened in the matter management system within 5 business days of Legal becoming aware of it, with assigned counsel, opposing parties, jurisdiction, and an initial exposure assessment. Off-system matters are prohibited, and matters meeting materiality thresholds are flagged for Finance reserve evaluation and disclosure review.

items.name: Approved Panel
items.description: Outside work is placed with firms on the Legal-maintained approved panel, selected for insurance-sector expertise, jurisdictional coverage, rates, and conflict posture. Off-panel engagements require General Counsel approval with documented rationale, and the panel is formally reviewed at least every two years against performance and spend data.

items.name: Billing Guidelines
items.description: All panel firms are bound by ABC Insurance Group's outside counsel billing guidelines, which set task-based billing requirements, staffing expectations, non-billable activities, and expense rules. Guidelines are incorporated into every engagement, and repeated violations are grounds for fee adjustment or panel removal.

items.name: Budget Tracking
items.description: Significant matters carry a phase-based budget agreed with outside counsel at the outset and revised at major case milestones. Actual fees and costs are tracked against budget in the e-billing system, and projected overruns above 15% require written justification and in-house counsel approval before further spend.

items.name: Custodian Acknowledgment Tracked
items.description: Each custodian must affirmatively acknowledge the hold, and acknowledgments are tracked in the matter management system with escalation to the custodian's manager after 5 business days of non-response. Holds are re-confirmed periodically for long-running matters, custodian lists are updated as employees join or leave, and releases are issued in writing only when Legal closes the preservation obligation.

items.name: Engagement Letters
items.description: Each new firm relationship, and each significant new matter, is governed by an executed engagement letter specifying scope, staffing, rates, conflict and confidentiality terms, and data-handling obligations appropriate to policyholder information. No work may begin or be paid without the engagement letter on file.

items.name: Hold Notice Within 24 Hours of Trigger
items.description: When Legal identifies a preservation trigger, such as a suit, demand letter, regulatory subpoena, or a claim flagged for bad-faith exposure, a written hold notice is issued to identified custodians and to IT within 24 hours. The notice describes the matter, the categories of records to preserve, including emails, claim files, underwriting files, and recorded calls, and suspends routine deletion for affected data sources.

items.name: Invoice Review
items.description: Firm invoices are submitted through the e-billing system, where automated rules and reviewing attorneys check them against guidelines, budgets, and the work actually performed. Non-compliant line items are adjusted or rejected with reasons returned to the firm, and approved invoices route to payment within agreed terms.

items.name: Monthly Status Updates
items.description: Responsible attorneys record a substantive status entry for each active matter at least monthly, covering recent developments, upcoming deadlines, and any change in exposure or strategy. These updates feed the litigation report provided to the General Counsel and support quarterly loss-contingency reviews with Finance and external auditors.

items.name: Approval Workflow
items.description: Completed assessments route through a defined workflow for privacy counsel review, with Information Security and Compliance sign-off where their domains are implicated. Processing may not begin until approval is recorded, and conditions attached to approval are tracked to closure by the project owner.

items.name: DPA Required for Vendors Handling Personal Data
items.description: No vendor, TPA, MGA, or other service provider may receive or process personal data until a data processing agreement or equivalent addendum is executed. The requirement applies regardless of contract value and covers data such as claims files, medical records, and producer-collected applicant information, consistent with obligations under GLBA, HIPAA where applicable, and state insurance data security laws modeled on the NAIC standard.

items.name: Documented DSR Process
items.description: A written procedure defines how requests are received across channels including web forms, call centers, and agents, how requester identity is verified, and how data is located across policy administration, claims, and marketing systems. The procedure also addresses insurance-specific exceptions, such as records that must be retained for claims handling, fraud investigation, or statutory record-keeping despite a deletion request.

items.name: Logging Required
items.description: Every request is logged with receipt date, requester category, verification outcome, actions taken, and response date, creating an auditable record of rights fulfillment. The log is reviewed quarterly for timeliness and volume trends and serves as primary evidence in regulatory examinations and inquiries.

items.name: PIA Required for New Processing
items.description: A privacy impact assessment must be completed before launching any new or materially changed processing of personal data, including new systems, vendor integrations, data sharing arrangements, and models that score or profile consumers. Projects subject to heightened regulatory scrutiny, such as algorithmic underwriting or use of sensitive health data, automatically require a full assessment.

items.name: Response Within Regulatory Timeline
items.description: Each request is responded to within the deadline of the applicable statute, typically 45 days under state consumer privacy laws, with extensions invoked and communicated only as the law permits. Internal milestones are set ahead of the legal deadline, and at-risk requests are escalated to the privacy officer before the date is missed.

items.name: Review Process
items.description: Negotiated DPAs are reviewed by privacy counsel in coordination with Information Security, which validates that promised technical and organizational measures match the vendor's actual assessment results. Approved DPAs are linked to the master agreement in the CLM and re-examined when the scope of data sharing materially changes.

items.name: Standard Clauses
items.description: Legal maintains standard DPA language covering processing limitations, confidentiality, security controls, breach notification within defined timeframes, subprocessor restrictions, audit rights, and return or destruction of data at termination. The standard terms are updated as state privacy laws and regulatory expectations evolve, and counterparty-proposed alternatives are measured against them.

items.name: Standardized Template
items.description: Assessments use the privacy office's standard template, which captures data elements and sources, purposes, legal basis, retention, third-party transfers, and identified risks with mitigations. The uniform format makes assessments comparable across business lines and ready for production to regulators on request.

items.name: Coordination with Business
items.description: The coordinating attorney works with the affected business units, such as Claims, Underwriting, or Distribution, to gather accurate facts and records, and validates business-drafted content before it goes to the regulator. Business stakeholders are briefed on inquiry status and on any remediation commitments made in the response.

items.name: Filing Calendar
items.description: All recurring regulatory filings, including holding company filings such as Form B and enterprise risk reports, state corporate registrations, and Legal-owned components of financial and market conduct submissions, are maintained on a centralized compliance calendar. Each entry carries due dates, lead times, and automated reminders, and the calendar is reconciled annually against current statutory requirements in every licensed state.

items.name: Ownership Assigned
items.description: Every filing has a named preparer and a named accountable owner responsible for on-time, accurate submission, with documented backups to cover absences and turnover. Ownership changes are updated on the calendar immediately, and unowned filings are treated as a control deficiency reported to the General Counsel.

items.name: Privilege Review
items.description: Documents and draft responses are reviewed for attorney-client privilege and work product before production, with privileged materials withheld or logged as the situation requires. Counsel also evaluates confidentiality protections available for produced materials, such as state exam confidentiality statutes and trade secret designations.

items.name: Response Protocol
items.description: All regulatory inquiries, including DOI consumer complaint referrals, data calls, exam requests, and subpoenas, are routed to Legal upon receipt and logged in the matter management system. The protocol designates a single coordinating attorney per inquiry, defines who may communicate with the regulator, and prohibits business units from responding directly without Legal clearance.

items.name: Retention Requirements
items.description: As-filed copies, regulator acknowledgments, and supporting workpapers are retained under the records retention schedule and remain readily retrievable for state examinations. Retention periods meet or exceed the longest applicable statutory requirement across the jurisdictions where the filing was made.

items.name: Review Process
items.description: Filings undergo a second-person review proportionate to their significance before submission, with material filings, such as those affecting the holding company structure or regulatory commitments, reviewed by senior counsel. Reviewers verify accuracy, consistency with prior filings, and proper signatory authority.

items.name: Timeline Tracking
items.description: Regulator deadlines and any granted extensions are docketed with internal due dates set in advance of the official date. Aging open inquiries are reviewed at least monthly, and any response at risk of missing a regulatory deadline is escalated to the General Counsel before the deadline passes.

items.name: Annual Updates
items.description: Training content is refreshed at least annually to reflect new statutes, regulatory developments, and lessons learned from internal incidents and examinations, and employees complete recertification on the updated material each year. Completion rates are tracked by HR and reported to the General Counsel, with follow-up for delinquent employees and their managers.

items.name: Compliance Awareness
items.description: General awareness training covers the legal topics most likely to arise in an insurance carrier's daily operations, including privacy and safeguarding of policyholder information, litigation holds and records preservation, unfair trade practice basics, and when to escalate to Legal. Content is tailored by role, with deeper modules for claims, underwriting, and distribution staff.

items.name: Contract Basics for Business
items.description: Employees who request, negotiate, or manage contracts complete training on the contracting lifecycle, including when Legal review is required, how to use approved templates and the CLM, signature authority limits, and the risks of side agreements or verbal commitments. Completion is required before an employee is granted contract-initiation access in the CLM.

items.name: Aging Follow-Up Cadence
items.description: Outstanding balances are worked on a defined schedule tied to aging buckets, with documented contact attempts at 30, 60, and 90 days past due. Collections staff record each touch in the billing system so that account history supports any subsequent action and aging reports reflect genuine collection effort.

items.name: Disputes Resolved Within 5 Business Days
items.description: When a policyholder or producer challenges a billed amount, the dispute is investigated, corrected or explained, and closed within five business days of receipt. Adjustments such as premium reversals or fee waivers are documented with supporting rationale, and disputed amounts are suspended from collections activity while under review.

items.name: Dunning Letter Schedule
items.description: A standardized sequence of dunning notices is issued at fixed intervals as a balance ages, using approved letter templates that meet state notice-content requirements. Timing and wording escalate progressively, from a courtesy reminder through formal demand, and every letter generated is retained on the account record.

items.name: Escalation Thresholds
items.description: Dollar-amount and aging triggers determine when an account moves to supervisory review, referral to an external collection agency, or cancellation for non-payment. Thresholds are documented and applied uniformly across lines of business, and any deviation requires manager approval recorded against the account.

items.name: Invoice Accuracy Above 99.5%
items.description: Issued invoices must reflect the correct premium, fees, taxes, and payment plan at least 99.5% of the time, measured through periodic sampling against policy administration records. Results are reported monthly, and any breach of the threshold triggers a root-cause review of rating, endorsement, or billing-system feeds.

items.name: Same-Day Cash Application Target
items.description: Payments received through lockbox, electronic funds transfer, card, or agency sweep are posted to the correct policy account on the business day they are received. Posting timeliness is tracked daily, and any backlog carried overnight is reported to billing management with a clearance plan.

items.name: Suspense Items Cleared Within 48 Hours
items.description: Funds that cannot be matched to a policy at receipt are placed in suspense and researched immediately, with identification and application completed within 48 hours. Items that cannot be resolved in that window are escalated, and the suspense account is reconciled regularly so unapplied cash never masks a delinquency or distorts receivables.

items.name: Alternate Site Capability
items.description: The department maintains the ability to shift servicing work to an alternate location or to remote-work arrangements, with sufficient seats, telephony routing, and system access to sustain critical policyholder service levels. Capacity assumptions are validated as part of annual testing.

items.name: Annual Testing
items.description: Each plan is exercised at least once a year through tabletop simulations or live failover tests, including scenarios such as contact-center outages during a catastrophe event. Test results, gaps, and remediation actions are documented and tracked to closure before the next cycle.

items.name: Communication Protocols
items.description: Predefined call trees and notification procedures cover employees, leadership, regulators, vendors, and distribution partners during a disruption. Protocols specify who declares an event, how policyholders are informed of service impacts, and how status updates are issued until normal operations resume.

items.name: Documented Plans
items.description: Business continuity and disaster recovery plans are maintained in writing for every critical operations and customer service function, identifying recovery time objectives, key personnel, system dependencies, and step-by-step recovery procedures. Plans are reviewed and updated whenever processes, systems, or staffing models change materially.

items.name: Acknowledgment Sent
items.description: The complainant receives a written or verbal acknowledgment confirming the complaint was received, who owns it, and the expected response timeframe. Acknowledgments for regulator-forwarded complaints follow the specific deadlines set by the originating state insurance department.

items.name: Complaint Logged Within 24 Hours
items.description: Every complaint, whether received by phone, mail, email, or through a department of insurance, is entered into the complaint register within 24 hours of receipt. The log captures the complainant, policy, line of business, nature of the grievance, and receipt channel, providing the data foundation for regulatory complaint reporting.

items.name: Escalation Criteria Defined
items.description: Written criteria specify which matters must be escalated, including regulator involvement, threatened litigation, allegations of agent misconduct, repeat complaints, and issues exceeding defined dollar thresholds. Front-line staff are trained on the criteria so escalation decisions do not depend on individual judgment alone.

items.name: Management Notification
items.description: Escalated items are routed to the designated management tier within a set timeframe, with department of insurance complaints and potential legal matters also flagged to compliance or legal counsel. Notifications include a summary of the issue, actions taken to date, and the response deadline.

items.name: Resolution Authority
items.description: Each escalation level carries documented authority limits for remedies such as fee waivers, premium adjustments, goodwill payments, and policy reinstatements. Decisions made under that authority are recorded with rationale, and matters exceeding a level's limits move upward rather than being settled out of grade.

items.name: Resolution Tracked
items.description: Each complaint is tracked through to closure with its investigation findings, the response provided, and any corrective action recorded. Aging open complaints are reviewed by management, and closed-complaint data is trended by cause and business area to identify systemic service issues.

items.name: Destruction Protocols
items.description: Records that have passed their retention period and carry no legal hold are destroyed through approved secure methods, with certificates of destruction retained for physical media and verified deletion for electronic records. Destruction events are logged and approved before execution, never performed ad hoc.

items.name: Indexing Standards
items.description: Incoming and generated documents are classified and indexed against a standard taxonomy, with required metadata such as policy number, document type, line of business, and receipt date applied at capture. Indexing accuracy is sampled periodically because misfiled documents undermine both service and discovery obligations.

items.name: Retention Schedules
items.description: Records are kept for the periods required by the corporate retention schedule and applicable state insurance regulations, which vary by record type and jurisdiction. Legal holds suspend normal retention for affected records, and the schedule itself is reviewed against regulatory change.

items.name: Retrieval SLA
items.description: Indexed documents must be retrievable within a defined service level, with same-day or faster turnaround for active service requests, claims support, and regulator demands. Retrieval performance is measured, and failures are analyzed for indexing or storage-system root causes.

items.name: Annual Review Cycle
items.description: Each SOP is reviewed at least annually by its designated owner to confirm it still reflects current systems, regulations, and practice, with off-cycle updates required when a material change occurs sooner. Review completion is tracked, and overdue procedures are escalated to department management.

items.name: Benefits Measured
items.description: Every implemented improvement is evaluated against a pre-stated baseline, quantifying gains in cycle time, cost, quality, or customer satisfaction. Realized benefits are validated after a settling period and reported to leadership, distinguishing projected savings from results actually achieved.

items.name: Improvement Ideas Tracked
items.description: Suggestions from employees, quality reviews, and complaint trends are captured in a single improvement backlog with an owner, status, and disposition for each idea. The backlog is reviewed on a regular cadence so submissions are visibly actioned or closed with feedback to the contributor.

items.name: Kaizen and Lean Initiatives
items.description: The department runs structured improvement events using Lean and Kaizen methods, targeting high-volume servicing processes such as endorsements, billing inquiries, and correspondence handling. Events follow a defined charter, involve the staff who perform the work, and conclude with implemented changes rather than recommendations alone.

items.name: Metrics Identified
items.description: Every mapped process has defined performance measures covering volume, cycle time, quality, and cost, with stated data sources and calculation methods. These metrics feed the department's operational reporting and provide the baseline against which improvement work is judged.

items.name: Process Maps Maintained
items.description: Current-state maps exist for each key operational process, showing steps, handoffs, systems touched, and decision points from intake to completion. Maps are refreshed whenever a process or supporting system changes, so documentation never drifts from how work is genuinely performed.

items.name: RACI Defined
items.description: Each documented process carries a RACI matrix assigning who is responsible, accountable, consulted, and informed for every major step, including handoffs to underwriting, claims, and IT. Accountability gaps and overlaps surfaced by the matrix are resolved by process owners rather than left ambiguous.

items.name: SOPs for All Key Processes
items.description: Step-level written procedures exist for every key process, including policy changes, billing transactions, document handling, and complaint intake, detailing system steps, state-specific variations, and exception handling. New or changed processes may not go live without an approved SOP in place.

items.name: Version Control
items.description: SOPs are held in a controlled repository where each revision carries a version number, effective date, change summary, and approver. Superseded versions are archived rather than deleted, allowing the department to demonstrate which procedure was in force at any point in time during an audit or examination.

items.name: Accuracy Targets Above 99%
items.description: Reviewed transactions must meet or exceed 99% accuracy, with critical defects, such as wrong coverage amounts, incorrect effective dates, or misapplied payments, weighted more heavily than cosmetic errors. Teams or individuals falling below target operate under documented remediation plans until performance recovers.

items.name: Closed-Loop Feedback
items.description: Detractor responses and serious dissatisfaction signals trigger outreach to the customer within a defined window to resolve the underlying issue. Outcomes of that outreach, along with systemic fixes driven by survey insight, are tracked to completion and reported so the loop demonstrably closes.

items.name: Coaching Documented
items.description: Evaluation results are reviewed with each agent in documented coaching sessions that record strengths, specific gaps, and agreed actions. Repeated failures on compliance-critical elements, such as missed disclosures or privacy verification, trigger formal performance follow-up rather than coaching alone.

items.name: Errors Tracked and Trended
items.description: Every defect found in review is logged with its type, root cause, responsible process, and correction status, and identified errors are fixed on the affected policy, not just counted. Error data is trended monthly to expose patterns by transaction type, processor, or system, feeding targeted training and process changes.

items.name: Five Calls per Agent per Month Monitored
items.description: Quality analysts or supervisors evaluate a minimum of five recorded or live calls for every agent each month, drawn across call types and times of day rather than cherry-picked. Monitoring volume is tracked, and shortfalls for any agent are made up in the following period.

items.name: Five Percent Sample Reviewed
items.description: At least five percent of completed transactions in each work type are independently re-checked by quality reviewers against source documents and system entries. Samples are selected randomly within each processor and transaction category so results fairly represent the whole population of work.

items.name: NPS Tracking
items.description: Net Promoter Score is measured on a defined cadence for both transactional touchpoints and the broader relationship, segmented by line of business and service channel. Scores are trended against targets and prior periods, and material movements prompt investigation rather than passive reporting.

items.name: Post-Interaction Surveys
items.description: Customers are invited to rate their experience shortly after service interactions across phone, email, chat, and policy-change transactions. Survey design, sampling, and channel coverage are governed so results are representative, and response data flows back to teams at the agent and queue level.

items.name: Quality Scorecard
items.description: Each monitored call is scored against a standardized scorecard covering accuracy of information given, adherence to required disclosures and verification procedures, system documentation, and customer experience behaviors. Scorecard criteria are calibrated regularly among evaluators so scoring stays consistent across the team.

items.name: Verbatim Analysis
items.description: Free-text survey comments are systematically categorized by theme, such as billing confusion, claim status frustration, or hold times, using consistent coding so themes can be quantified. Recurring verbatim themes are matched against complaint and quality data to confirm whether they reflect genuine process defects.

items.name: Daily Dashboard
items.description: An operational dashboard is published each business day showing intake volumes, service levels, backlog and inventory aging, and staffing against plan for the contact center and processing teams. Supervisors use it to rebalance work and flag same-day risks to service commitments.

items.name: Monthly Business Review
items.description: Department leadership conducts a monthly review covering full operational performance, complaint and satisfaction results, vendor performance, expense position, and progress on improvement initiatives. Decisions and action items from the review are minuted and tracked through to the following session.

items.name: Trend Analysis
items.description: Key operational measures are analyzed over rolling multi-month horizons to distinguish seasonal patterns, such as renewal-driven call peaks or catastrophe surges, from genuine performance shifts. Trend findings inform staffing forecasts, capacity planning, and the prioritization of improvement work.

items.name: Weekly Scorecard
items.description: A weekly scorecard rolls daily results into performance against SLA, quality, and productivity targets, with red, amber, and green status against each goal. Misses carry a brief owner commentary explaining cause and corrective action rather than appearing as unexplained numbers.

items.name: 80% of Calls Answered in 30 Seconds
items.description: The contact center maintains a grade of service in which at least 80% of inbound calls reach a live agent within 30 seconds of entering the queue. Performance is measured at interval level throughout the day, not just as a daily average, so peak-period failures cannot hide inside aggregate numbers.

items.name: Abandonment Rate Below 5%
items.description: Fewer than 5% of queued callers may hang up before reaching an agent, measured net of very short abandons. Sustained breaches trigger review of staffing, IVR routing, and queue messaging, since abandoned calls frequently resurface as complaints or lost retention.

items.name: Average Handle Time Targets by Call Type
items.description: Handle-time expectations are set separately for each call category, recognizing that a billing inquiry, a policy endorsement, and a first notice of loss demand different durations.
