Targets are derived from observed performance of competent handling rather than imposed arbitrarily, and they are managed as a balance against quality and first-call resolution, never at their expense.

items.name: Cancellations per State Requirements
items.description: Policy cancellations and nonrenewals are executed in strict accordance with each state's notice periods, permissible grounds, delivery methods, and proof-of-mailing requirements, which override any internal turnaround target. Compliance is verified through quality sampling, since a defective cancellation can leave the carrier on risk or expose it to regulatory action.

items.name: Certificates Same Day
items.description: Certificates of insurance requested by insureds, agents, or third parties such as lenders and contract counterparties are produced and delivered the same business day. Certificate content is generated from current policy data to guarantee evidence of coverage is accurate at issuance.

items.name: Chat Wait Time Under 2 Minutes
items.description: Customers initiating a chat session are connected to a live agent in less than two minutes on average, with concurrency limits set so agents handling multiple chats can still respond promptly within each session. Wait-time performance is monitored in real time and staffing is adjusted intraday when queues build.

items.name: Email Response Within 4 Hours
items.description: Customer and producer emails receive a substantive reply within four business hours of receipt, not merely an automated acknowledgment. Response timeliness is measured from arrival in the service queue, and aging items are escalated before the window expires.

items.name: Endorsements Within 48 Hours
items.description: Requested policy changes, such as added vehicles, coverage adjustments, or address updates, are processed and issued within 48 hours of receiving a complete request. Endorsements needing underwriting referral are flagged and tracked separately so the standard turnaround is preserved for routine changes.

items.name: First Contact Resolution Above 70%
items.description: More than 70% of email and chat inquiries are resolved in the initial interaction without transfer, callback, or repeat contact on the same issue. Resolution is verified through repeat-contact tracking and survey confirmation, and inquiry types that routinely fail first-contact handling are targeted for knowledge-base or process fixes.

items.name: Competency Assessments
items.description: Trainees must pass knowledge checks and practical evaluations, such as graded simulated calls or test transactions, before progressing through and graduating from training. Assessment results are recorded, and individuals who do not meet the standard receive remediation or extended training rather than early release to production work.

items.name: Compliance Refreshers
items.description: All servicing staff complete recurring training on privacy and information security, unfair trade practices, complaint identification, anti-fraud awareness, and other regulatory obligations on at least an annual cycle. Completion is tracked to the individual, and overdue refreshers are escalated because evidence of training is routinely requested in market-conduct examinations.

items.name: Nesting Period
items.description: Following classroom training, new hires work live volume in a supervised nesting environment with reduced workload expectations, immediate access to coaches, and heightened quality monitoring. Graduation from nesting depends on meeting defined quality and proficiency gates, not simply on elapsed time.

items.name: Product Updates
items.description: Staff receive timely training whenever products, coverage forms, rates, or rules change across the carrier's P&C, life and retirement, and group benefits lines. Training is delivered before the change takes effect in the market, so agents never field customer questions about products they have not been briefed on.

items.name: Role-Specific Curriculum
items.description: Each role follows a defined training curriculum covering the products and lines of business it will service, core systems, state-specific servicing rules, privacy and disclosure requirements, and the procedures for its transaction types. Curricula are maintained alongside SOPs so training content reflects current practice.

items.name: Soft Skills
items.description: Periodic development sessions address communication, empathy, de-escalation, and handling of difficult or vulnerable customers, with content informed by call quality findings and complaint themes. These skills are reinforced through coaching rather than treated as one-time classroom events.

items.name: System Changes
items.description: Releases affecting the policy administration, billing, telephony, or document systems are accompanied by training and updated job aids delivered ahead of go-live. Post-implementation support is provided during the adoption period, and recurring user errors after a release feed back into supplemental training.

items.name: Audit Rights
items.description: Contracts reserve the carrier's right to audit vendor operations, controls, security, and records, including on-site inspection and regulator access, consistent with insurance outsourcing expectations. Audit rights are actually exercised on a risk-based schedule, and findings are remediated under tracked plans rather than noted and shelved.

items.name: Governance Meetings
items.description: A structured governance cadence pairs regular operational reviews of volumes, performance, and issues with periodic executive sessions covering the relationship, commercial matters, and strategic direction. Meetings produce minuted decisions and action logs that are tracked between sessions.

items.name: Performance Monitoring
items.description: Vendor output is measured continuously against the contracted SLAs through vendor-submitted reporting validated by independent carrier-side sampling of completed work. Persistent underperformance triggers formal corrective action plans with defined cure periods and consequences.

items.name: SLAs Defined
items.description: Every BPO engagement operates under contractual service level agreements covering turnaround times, quality and accuracy thresholds, availability, and data-handling obligations, with remedies or credits specified for misses. SLAs mirror the standards applied to equivalent in-house work so customers experience no difference by sourcing model.

items.name: Backup Coverage Plans
items.description: Every critical function and key-person dependency has a named backup arrangement, ensuring time-sensitive work such as cancellations, regulatory correspondence, and cash application continues through vacancies, leave, and surge events. Coverage plans are tested in practice, not maintained as paper designations.

items.name: Cross-Training Requirements
items.description: A defined share of staff in each function must be trained and kept proficient in at least one additional work type, with skill currency maintained through periodic refreshers and rotational live work. The resulting skill matrix is documented so leaders know exactly who can flex where when volumes shift.

items.name: Forecast Accuracy
items.description: Contact and transaction volumes are forecast at interval, daily, and seasonal horizons, incorporating drivers such as renewal cycles, billing runs, and catastrophe activity. Forecast accuracy is measured against actuals with defined variance tolerances, and persistent misses drive recalibration of the forecasting model.

items.name: Overtime Approval
items.description: Overtime is authorized in advance by designated approvers against documented business justification, rather than self-initiated by staff or used as a standing fix for understaffing. Overtime spend is tracked against budget and analyzed by cause, with recurring patterns redirected into the staffing plan.

items.name: Real-Time Management
items.description: Dedicated real-time monitoring watches queues, occupancy, and adherence throughout the day, triggering intraday actions such as skill reassignment, break adjustments, or deferral of offline work when service levels are threatened. Intraday decisions and their outcomes are logged to improve future response playbooks.

items.name: Schedule Adherence
items.description: Agents are expected to work their published schedules within a defined adherence threshold, with conformance tracked through the workforce management system. Adherence results are reviewed in coaching, recognizing that even fully staffed days fail service levels when staff are off-plan at the interval level.

items.name: Staffing Ratios
items.description: Documented ratios govern staffing relative to workload drivers, including agents per supervisor, quality reviewers per production team, and headcount per forecast volume by function. Ratios are reviewed against service and quality outcomes and adjusted through the planning cycle rather than eroded silently through unfilled vacancies.

items.name: Acceptance Criteria
items.description: Each story carries explicit, testable acceptance criteria agreed with the product owner before planning. Criteria must describe observable behavior so testers and developers share one definition of success.

items.name: Accepted
items.description: The product owner has reviewed the working functionality against the acceptance criteria and formally accepted it in the work management tool. Acceptance is the final gate before the story contributes to velocity.

items.name: Capacity Planning
items.description: Velocity is reconciled with actual team capacity each sprint, adjusting for planned leave, holidays, production support rotations, and onboarding. Capacity-adjusted forecasts are the basis for any external delivery date communicated to stakeholders.

items.name: Code Complete
items.description: All development work for the item is finished, merged to the integration branch, and free of known unfinished stubs or TODO placeholders. Partial implementations may not be carried forward into a subsequent sprint under the same story.

items.name: Consistent Start and End Days
items.description: Sprints begin and end on the same weekdays enterprise-wide, allowing program-level events, dependency syncs, and reporting cycles to be scheduled against a common boundary.

items.name: Dependencies Identified
items.description: Upstream and cross-team dependencies, including those on policy administration, claims, or shared data platforms, are identified and recorded on the item before commitment. Dependent teams must have acknowledged the need or the item stays in refinement.

items.name: Deployable
items.description: The change builds cleanly in the CI pipeline and can be promoted to production without manual intervention beyond the standard release process. Items that require unscheduled environment work or unresolved configuration are not done.

items.name: Documented
items.description: Relevant documentation is updated alongside the change, including technical design notes, runbooks, API references, and any user-facing or operations material affected. Documentation updates are part of the story, not deferred follow-up work.

items.name: No Blockers
items.description: Known impediments such as pending access, unresolved design questions, or missing test data are cleared or have a dated resolution plan before the item is pulled into a sprint. Items with open blockers remain on the refinement backlog.

items.name: Reviewed
items.description: At least one qualified peer has completed a code review and recorded approval in the source control tool. Review comments classified as blocking must be addressed before merge.

items.name: Scrum Ceremonies
items.description: Requires every Scrum team to conduct the full set of ceremonies — Sprint Planning, Daily Standup, Sprint Review, and Retrospective — in line with the Scrum Guide, with consistent attendance, timeboxes, and recorded outcomes so that delivery rhythm and inspection points are uniform across teams.

items.name: Sized
items.description: The team has estimated the item using its agreed sizing method, and stories too large to complete within a single sprint are split before they enter planning.

items.name: Sprint Goals Documented
items.description: Every sprint carries a written sprint goal recorded in the work management tool at planning. The goal states the business outcome the sprint advances and is referenced at the sprint review to assess whether it was met.

items.name: Tested
items.description: The item has passed unit, integration, and applicable regression testing, with automated coverage added or updated for the changed behavior. Defects found during testing must be resolved or formally accepted by the product owner before the item closes.

items.name: Trend Monitored
items.description: Velocity trends are reviewed at retrospectives and in PMO health checks to detect sustained decline, volatility, or inflation. Significant shifts trigger a root-cause discussion rather than silent re-baselining.

items.name: Two-Week Sprints
items.description: All Scrum teams operate on a two-week sprint length. Deviations require PMO approval and are limited to teams with a documented operational constraint, such as regulatory release windows.

items.name: Used for Planning
items.description: Sprint and release commitments are sized against the team's rolling average velocity, typically over the last three to six sprints. Commitments that materially exceed demonstrated velocity require explicit product owner sign-off and a stated rationale.

items.name: Velocity Calculated
items.description: Each team computes velocity every sprint from accepted story points only, using a consistent method maintained in the work management tool. Stories rejected or carried over do not count toward the sprint's velocity.

items.name: Approval Authority
items.description: Changes are approved at the level defined in the project's governance matrix, with thresholds based on cost and schedule impact. Requests exceeding the project manager's delegated authority escalate to the sponsor or steering committee.

items.name: Baseline Updates
items.description: Once approved, the project baseline, plan, and financial forecast are updated to reflect the change, and subsequent status reporting measures performance against the revised baseline. Superseded baselines are retained for audit traceability.

items.name: Change Request Process
items.description: Any proposed deviation from the approved baseline is documented as a formal change request in the PMO tool, with a unique identifier, requester, description, and justification. Verbal or email-only changes are not recognized.

items.name: Impact Assessment
items.description: Before a decision, each change request receives an assessment of its effect on scope, schedule, cost, resources, and risk, including downstream impact on regulatory commitments or dependent initiatives. The assessment is attached to the request record.

items.name: Deliverable Acceptance
items.description: All contracted deliverables are formally accepted in writing by the sponsor or designated business owner against the success criteria in the charter. Outstanding items are either accepted with documented exceptions or transferred to a named owner with a plan.

items.name: Knowledge Transfer
items.description: Operational documentation, support procedures, and system knowledge are handed over to the receiving run teams, with sign-off from the accepting manager. Transfer is complete only when the run organization confirms it can support the solution without project staff.

items.name: Lessons Learned
items.description: A lessons-learned session is held with the core team and key stakeholders before disbandment, and the findings are recorded in the PMO repository in a searchable form. Recurring themes are reported to the PMO for process improvement.

items.name: Resource Release
items.description: Project staff, contractors, and funded capacity are formally released on a communicated schedule, with assignments updated in the resource management system. Contractor end dates and access revocations are coordinated with vendor management and security.

items.name: Business Case Required
items.description: No initiative enters the portfolio without an approved business case covering the problem statement, expected benefits, cost estimate, and alignment to enterprise strategy. The depth of the case scales with investment size per the PMO's tiering guidance.

items.name: Capacity Validation
items.description: Intake confirms that the delivery teams, subject-matter experts, and funding needed for the request exist or can be sourced before approval. Requests that cannot be staffed are queued rather than approved into an over-committed portfolio.

items.name: Escalation Triggers
items.description: Predefined conditions, such as consecutive red statuses, budget variance beyond tolerance, or a missed regulatory milestone, automatically escalate an initiative to the board's exception agenda. Escalation is rule-driven and not subject to project-manager discretion.

items.name: Health Indicators
items.description: Every initiative is assessed against a standard set of health indicators spanning schedule, budget, scope, resourcing, and benefits confidence, using PMO-defined thresholds. Indicator definitions are uniform so initiatives can be compared on equal terms.

items.name: Monthly Portfolio Review
items.description: The portfolio governance board meets monthly to review all active initiatives, with a standard pack covering financials, delivery status, benefits, and risk. Attendance by accountable executives or their empowered delegates is mandatory.

items.name: Prioritization Criteria
items.description: Approved requests are scored against the portfolio's published prioritization criteria at intake so they enter the backlog with a defensible relative ranking. Criteria and weights are maintained by the portfolio governance board, not adjusted per request.

items.name: ROI Consideration
items.description: Expected financial return, including payback period and net benefit over the planning horizon, is a weighted factor in every ranking. Mandatory regulatory work is flagged separately so compliance obligations are not forced to compete on ROI alone.

items.name: Replanning Process
items.description: Initiatives that fail review may be directed into a structured replan covering revised scope, schedule, cost, and benefits, with a deadline for returning to the board. The board's options explicitly include pausing or terminating initiatives that no longer justify investment.

items.name: Resource Constraints
items.description: Final sequencing reflects real constraints on scarce skills, shared platforms, and change capacity in business operations. A high score does not guarantee immediate start if the required teams or environments are committed elsewhere.

items.name: Strategic Alignment
items.description: Scoring includes an explicit measure of how directly an initiative advances stated enterprise and business-line strategies, such as digital distribution, claims modernization, or retirement-business growth. Initiatives unable to map to a strategic objective receive the minimum alignment score.

items.name: Value Assessment
items.description: Each request is evaluated for quantified business value, whether expense reduction, premium growth, loss-ratio improvement, regulatory necessity, or risk mitigation. Value claims must identify the accountable business owner who will be measured on realization.

items.name: Weighted Scoring Model
items.description: All candidate initiatives are scored through a single weighted model with published criteria and weights approved by the portfolio governance board. Scores are recorded in the portfolio tool and refreshed when an initiative's assumptions materially change.

items.name: Approval Workflow
items.description: Gate decisions follow a defined workflow with named approvers, and the outcome, whether approved, approved with conditions, or held, is recorded in the PMO tool. Conditional approvals carry dated actions that are tracked to closure.

items.name: Assumptions and Constraints
items.description: Material assumptions, such as vendor availability or regulatory timelines, and binding constraints, such as fixed compliance dates or capped funding, are documented in the charter. Each is revisited during planning and converted to a risk if it proves uncertain.

items.name: Communication Plan
items.description: A communication plan identifies stakeholders, what information each group receives, the channel, and the frequency, from steering packs to frontline operations briefings. It also defines who may communicate externally where regulators, agents, or policyholders are affected.

items.name: Decisions Needed
items.description: The report states the specific decisions required from the sponsor or steering committee, the options considered, the recommendation, and the date by which a decision is needed to avoid impact. Stale undecided items escalate per the governance matrix.

items.name: Deliverable Checklist
items.description: A standard checklist of required artifacts, such as the approved design, test summary, or operational readiness assessment, is completed and evidenced before each gate. Missing artifacts must be waived in writing by the gate authority, with the waiver recorded.

items.name: Lessons Learned
items.description: Each gate review captures lessons from the completed phase while they are fresh, feeding both the project's own next phase and the PMO's cross-project knowledge base. Gate-level lessons supplement, not replace, the closure retrospective.

items.name: Milestones
items.description: The report shows progress against baselined milestones, including completed, upcoming, and slipped dates with revised forecasts. Movement of any regulatory or contractual milestone is highlighted explicitly.

items.name: Phase Gate Criteria
items.description: Each lifecycle phase has published entry and exit criteria maintained by the PMO, and a project may not advance until the exit criteria for its current phase are demonstrably met. Criteria cover delivery readiness, financial position, and risk posture.

items.name: RAG Status
items.description: Overall health and the schedule, budget, scope, and resource dimensions are each rated red, amber, or green against PMO-defined thresholds. Ratings reflect the defined criteria, and downgrades may not be suppressed or softened for audience comfort.

items.name: Resource Plan
items.description: The plan names the roles, skills, and allocation levels the project needs over time, including business SMEs from underwriting, claims, or actuarial functions whose availability is often the binding constraint. Confirmed commitments are recorded with the supplying managers.

items.name: Risk Register
items.description: A risk register is established during planning, seeded from the charter's assumptions and constraints and from PMO lessons on similar initiatives. The register is a living artifact reviewed on the project's standing governance cadence.

items.name: Risks and Issues
items.description: Top risks and open issues are summarized with their current severity, owner, and the action being taken, drawn directly from the project's RAID log. New high-severity entries since the prior report are called out.

items.name: Schedule or Roadmap
items.description: A baselined schedule with milestones and dependencies, or an equivalent release roadmap for agile delivery, is maintained in the approved planning tool. Key dates with regulatory or contractual force are flagged as fixed and protected through change control.

items.name: Scope Definition
items.description: The charter states what the project will and will not deliver, including affected products, channels, systems, and business units. Explicit out-of-scope statements are required to prevent later disputes over boundaries.

items.name: Sponsor Approval
items.description: The charter is signed by an accountable executive sponsor with authority over the affected business area and budget. Work beyond preliminary scoping may not start until sponsor approval is recorded.

items.name: Success Criteria
items.description: Measurable success criteria are defined at chartering, tied where possible to operational or financial metrics such as cycle time, expense ratio, or customer satisfaction. These criteria become the basis for deliverable acceptance and benefits tracking.

items.name: WBS or Backlog
items.description: The full scope is decomposed into either a work breakdown structure or a prioritized product backlog, depending on the delivery method. Every deliverable in the charter must trace to elements of this decomposition.

items.name: Weekly Status Report
items.description: Every active project issues a status report each week in the PMO's standard template, published in the portfolio tool by the agreed deadline. Reporting continues through quiet periods so absence of news is itself visible.

items.name: Actuals Versus Estimate Analysis
items.description: Project managers compare recorded actuals against estimates at least monthly, investigating variances beyond tolerance and feeding the findings into forecasts and future estimating models. Persistent estimation bias is surfaced to the PMO for calibration.

items.name: Allocation Visibility
items.description: Current and planned allocations for every delivery resource are maintained in the resource management system and visible to the PMO and supplying managers. Side arrangements that commit people outside the system are prohibited.

items.name: Conflict Resolution Process
items.description: When two or more initiatives compete for the same people or teams, the conflict is raised through a defined process that resolves it using portfolio priority order. Unresolved conflicts escalate to the portfolio governance board rather than being settled by informal negotiation.

items.name: Project and Task Level
items.description: Time is recorded against the specific project and task or workstream codes from the approved plan structure, not against generic buckets. This granularity supports accurate cost allocation and the capitalization treatment required for financial reporting.

items.name: Quarterly Capacity Forecast
items.description: Resource managers produce a rolling quarterly forecast of available capacity by team and skill group, net of run-the-business obligations, leave, and attrition assumptions. The forecast is reconciled against approved portfolio demand before each quarterly planning cycle.

items.name: Time Captured Weekly
items.description: All project staff, including contractors, submit time in the enterprise timekeeping system by the weekly cutoff, with manager approval following on the published schedule. Chronic late submission is reported to the PMO and the individual's manager.

items.name: Escalation Path
items.description: Issues that exceed the project manager's authority or breach their resolution date escalate along the documented path, from project manager to sponsor to steering committee. The escalation route and thresholds are defined in the project's governance plan at initiation.

items.name: Issue Logging
items.description: Any problem actively impacting scope, schedule, cost, or quality is recorded in the project's issue log within the governance tool, with a clear description, date raised, and severity. Issues discussed in meetings but never logged are treated as a process breach.

items.name: Mitigation Plans
items.description: Risks above the defined severity threshold require a documented response, whether mitigation, transfer, acceptance, or avoidance, with actions assigned to named owners and dates. Acceptance of a high-severity risk requires sponsor sign-off.

items.name: Ownership
items.description: Every open issue has a single named owner accountable for driving resolution, assigned at the point of logging. Ownership may transfer, but an issue may never sit unowned or be assigned to a group.

items.name: Probability and Impact Assessment
items.description: Each risk is scored for likelihood and consequence using the PMO's standard scales, producing a severity rating that drives review frequency and management attention. Impact assessment considers financial, schedule, regulatory, and reputational dimensions.

items.name: RAID Log
items.description: Risks, assumptions, issues, and dependencies are maintained together in a current RAID log within the governance tool, reviewed at least at every status cycle. The RAID log is the single authoritative record feeding status reports and gate reviews.

items.name: Risk Identification
items.description: Risks are actively identified throughout the project lifecycle, through planning workshops, standing team reviews, and triggers such as scope changes or vendor events. Anyone on the project may raise a risk, and identification is treated as a contribution rather than a criticism.

items.name: Target Resolution Date
items.description: Each issue carries a committed resolution date proportionate to its severity, and the date is tracked at the project's standing reviews. Slipped dates require a revised plan and an explanation, not silent extension.

items.name: Confidence Vote
items.description: The event closes with a confidence vote in which every participant rates the achievability of the plan. An average below the threshold triggers rework of the plan in the room before the train commits, and individual low votes are heard rather than overridden.

items.name: Cross-Team Dependencies Tracked
items.description: Dependencies between teams on the train, and with external parties such as platform, data, or vendor teams, are maintained on the ART planning board and reviewed at every sync. At-risk dependencies are renegotiated explicitly rather than discovered at the system demo.

items.name: Dependencies Identified
items.description: Teams surface dependencies on one another and on external groups during plan reviews and place them on the program board with agreed dates. A plan with unowned or unscheduled dependencies is not accepted as final.

items.name: Impediment Resolution
items.description: Impediments raised at the sync that cannot be resolved within a team are owned by the RTE and tracked on a visible impediment board until cleared. Items blocked beyond an agreed age escalate to the ART's leadership or Lean Portfolio Management.

items.name: Improvement Backlog Maintained
items.description: Agreed improvement actions are written as backlog items, entered into the ART backlog, and given capacity in the next PI plan. The RTE reports on the status of prior improvement items at the following Inspect and Adapt so actions cannot quietly evaporate.

items.name: Objectives Set
items.description: Each team drafts PI objectives describing the business outcomes it will deliver, and business owners assign value to them during the event. Committed and stretch objectives are distinguished, and the aggregated train objectives are published after the event.

items.name: PI Retrospective
items.description: Each train holds a PI-level retrospective as part of the Inspect and Adapt event, reviewing the PI system demo, objective achievement, and quantitative measures such as predictability. Participation spans teams, product management, and ART leadership.

items.name: Problem-Solving Workshop
items.description: The event includes a facilitated root-cause workshop on the most significant problems surfaced, using structured techniques such as fishbone analysis or five whys. Output is a small set of well-understood causes with proposed countermeasures, not a grievance list.

items.name: Quarterly PI Planning
items.description: Every Agile Release Train conducts a PI Planning event each quarter with all teams, product management, and business owners participating, in person or via the approved distributed format. The event follows the standard agenda, including business context, draft plan reviews, and management problem-solving.

items.name: Weekly ART Sync
items.description: The Release Train Engineer convenes a weekly sync combining the Scrum of Scrums and PO sync perspectives, attended by team representatives and product owners. The session reviews progress against PI objectives and adjusts plans where reality has diverged.

items.name: Invoicing
items.description: Vendor invoices are validated against the SOW, approved time records, and accepted milestones before payment is authorized by the budget owner. Discrepancies are disputed within the contractual window, and invoice status is reconciled in the project's financial tracking.

items.name: Milestone Tracking
items.description: Contractual milestones and deliverable due dates are loaded into the project plan and tracked alongside internal work, with formal acceptance recorded for each completed milestone. Slippage against contracted dates is reported in project status and assessed for remedy provisions.

items.name: Performance Monitoring
items.description: Vendor performance is reviewed on a regular cadence against agreed measures such as quality, responsiveness, staffing stability, and SLA attainment, with findings documented in the vendor governance record. Sustained underperformance triggers a corrective action plan with the supplier's account leadership.

items.name: Statement of Work and Contract Management
items.description: All vendor delivery work operates under an executed SOW or contract that defines deliverables, rates, acceptance terms, and key personnel, negotiated with procurement and reviewed by legal. Work beyond the contracted scope requires an amendment before it begins.

items.name: Clear Authority Levels by Premium, Limit, and Line of Business
items.description: Each underwriter's letter of authority specifies the maximum gross written premium, per-risk and aggregate limits, and the lines of business they may accept without escalation. Authority levels are reviewed at least annually and adjusted when an underwriter's role, performance, or portfolio results change. No risk may be accepted that exceeds any single dimension of the assigned authority, even if the others are within bounds.

items.name: Decision Documented Within 24 Hours
items.description: The receiving authority records an accept, decline, or conditional decision in the underwriting file within 24 hours of receiving a complete referral, including the rationale and any conditions imposed. Referrals that cannot be decided in that window are flagged with the reason and a committed decision date communicated back to the broker-facing underwriter.

items.name: Documented Referral Triggers
items.description: The matrix enumerates the specific conditions that force a referral upward, including premium or limit thresholds, hazardous classes, adverse loss history, non-standard terms, and out-of-appetite characteristics. Triggers are embedded in the underwriting workbench where feasible so they fire automatically rather than relying on underwriter recall, and the triggering condition is recorded in the file.

items.name: Only Authorized Personnel Can Bind
items.description: Coverage may be bound solely by individuals holding a current, written delegation of binding authority appropriate to the risk's premium, limit, and line of business. System access to issue binders is provisioned against the authority register, and any bind executed outside delegated authority is treated as an exception requiring immediate management review and ratification or rescission.

items.name: Referrals to Next Authority Level with Recommendation
items.description: A referral package must go to the next level in the authority matrix and include the referring underwriter's analysis and an explicit recommendation to accept, decline, or modify terms. Forwarding a file without a position is not an acceptable referral; the referring underwriter remains accountable for the quality of the supporting analysis.

items.name: Verbal Binders Documented Within 24 Hours
items.description: When market conditions require a verbal commitment to a broker, the binding underwriter must issue a written binder confirming insured, coverage, limits, premium, effective date, and any subjectivities within 24 hours. The written confirmation is attached to the underwriting file, and unconfirmed verbal binders are escalated to underwriting management for resolution.

items.name: All Insureds Screened Before Binding
items.description: Named insureds, and where applicable beneficial owners and additional insureds, are screened against the current OFAC SDN list and other applicable sanctions lists before any binder or policy is issued. Potential matches are routed to Compliance for disposition, and binding is held until the match is cleared or the risk is declined.

items.name: Current Form Filings
items.description: Only policy forms and endorsements that are filed and approved, or properly exempt, in the state of issue may be attached to a policy. Underwriting maintains form libraries in the policy administration system synchronized with the filing inventory, and withdrawn or superseded forms are deactivated so they cannot be issued in error.

items.name: Ongoing Monitoring for Renewals
items.description: The in-force book is rescreened as sanctions lists are updated, and every renewal passes through screening again before terms are released. A hit on an existing insured triggers immediate referral to Compliance, suspension of payments where required by law, and regulatory reporting in accordance with OFAC blocking and rejection rules.

items.name: Rate Filings Approved Before Use
items.description: Filed rates, rating plans, and rule manuals must have the required state approval or effective filing status before they are applied to new or renewal business. New rate levels are not loaded into rating engines ahead of their approved effective dates, and use-and-file jurisdictions follow the documented filing timeline.

items.name: Surplus Lines Compliance
items.description: Risks placed through the company's surplus lines paper must satisfy state eligibility and diligent search requirements, be transacted through a licensed surplus lines broker, and carry the required disclosures and stamping. Underwriters confirm the placement basis is documented in the file before binding non-admitted business.

items.name: Actuarial Review for Large Accounts
items.description: Accounts exceeding the defined large-account threshold receive an actuarial review of exposure, loss development, and proposed pricing before the quote is released. The actuary's indicated price and the underwriter's selected price are both recorded, and material gaps between them must be explained and approved at the appropriate authority level.

items.name: Audit Trail Maintained
items.description: The pricing system preserves a complete record of the technical rate, each deviation applied, the approver, and the timestamp, so the final premium can be reconstructed end to end. These records are retained per the corporate retention schedule and made available to Internal Audit, actuarial monitoring, and market conduct examiners.

items.name: Deviation from Filed Rates per Authority Matrix
items.description: Any credit, debit, or departure from the filed or technical rate must fall within the deviation bands granted to the underwriter in the authority matrix. Deviations beyond the assigned band require referral to the next authority level before the quote is released, and aggregate deviation usage is monitored at the portfolio level.

items.name: Documentation Required
items.description: Every deviation is supported by a written justification in the file that ties the adjustment to identifiable risk characteristics, competitive intelligence, or account considerations. Unsupported or boilerplate justifications are treated as documentation failures in quality review.

items.name: Filed Rates Applied Correctly
items.description: Underwriters and rating systems must apply the filed base rates, classifications, territories, and rating factors exactly as approved, with classification decisions supported by the information in the file. Misclassification and manual overrides of system-calculated rates are tracked as rating errors and corrected through endorsement where discovered.

items.name: Loss Ratio Targets by Line of Business
items.description: Actuarial establishes target loss ratios for each line of business, and underwriters price individual accounts against those targets rather than against market rate alone. Performance versus target is reviewed in regular portfolio meetings, and persistent adverse variance triggers corrective pricing or appetite action.

items.name: Mandatory Pricing Tool Usage
items.description: All eligible accounts must be rated through the approved pricing tool so that the technical premium, selected premium, and rate adequacy ratio are captured consistently. Off-tool pricing is permitted only for documented system limitations and requires manager sign-off with the manual calculation attached to the file.

items.name: Minimum Premium Enforced
items.description: No policy may be issued below the minimum premium established for its line of business and program, regardless of credits or competitive pressure. Rating systems enforce the floor automatically, and any exception requires documented approval from underwriting management.

items.name: Schedule Rating Documented
items.description: Where schedule rating credits or debits are applied, the file must identify the specific risk characteristics supporting each modification and stay within the maximums allowed by the filed plan. Generic or unsupported schedule modifications are not permitted and are a standing focus of underwriting audit.

items.name: Annual Audit by Internal Audit
items.description: Internal Audit performs an independent review of the underwriting function at least annually, testing adherence to authority limits, referral discipline, pricing standards, and file documentation. Findings are formally reported with agreed remediation owners and dates, and open items are tracked to closure through the audit committee process.

items.name: File Documentation
items.description: Every bound account must carry a complete underwriting file containing the application, the risk analysis worksheet, the rationale for the selected pricing, and evidence of all required approvals, so that a reviewer can reconstruct why the risk was accepted on its terms without consulting the underwriter. Incomplete files are treated as quality defects subject to remediation timelines.

items.name: Monthly 5% Sample Review by Underwriting Management
items.description: Each month, underwriting management reviews a sample of at least 5% of bound accounts per underwriter against the quality checklist, scoring risk selection, rating accuracy, and documentation. Results feed individual coaching and authority decisions, and recurring deficiencies escalate to the chief underwriting officer.

items.name: Peer Review
items.description: Accounts generating more than $100,000 in premium must be reviewed by a second qualified underwriter before binding, with the reviewer assessing risk selection, terms, and pricing independently of the handling underwriter. The peer reviewer's concurrence or noted concerns are documented in the file, adding a structured second set of eyes on the accounts that carry the greatest potential to move portfolio results.

items.name: Non-Renewal Notice per State Requirement
items.description: When the company elects not to renew, conditional or final notice is issued within each state's statutory notice period and in the form the state prescribes, including required reasons where mandated. Notice generation is calendared against the longest applicable state requirement, and proof of mailing or delivery is retained in the file.

items.name: Quote to Broker 60 Days Out
items.description: Renewal terms, conditions, and premium are released to the broker no later than 60 days before expiration for accounts the company intends to retain. Late quotes are tracked as a service metric, and accounts that cannot be quoted on time are escalated to management with the cause documented.

items.name: Renewal Review 90 Days Out
items.description: The handling underwriter begins the renewal evaluation no later than 90 days before expiration, refreshing exposure data, loss experience, and appetite fit, and ordering any updated inspections or financials needed. The intended renewal strategy, including restructure or non-renewal candidates, is identified at this point so downstream deadlines can be met.

items.name: Retention Rate Targets by Segment
items.description: Management sets policy-count and premium retention targets for each segment of the book, weighted toward the accounts the company most wants to keep. Actual retention is reported against target monthly, and segments running below plan receive a documented action plan covering pricing posture, service issues, or broker engagement.

items.name: Win-Back Process for Lost Accounts
items.description: Lost accounts that fit appetite are logged with the reason for loss, the competing carrier and terms where known, and a follow-up date ahead of the next renewal cycle. Targeted win-back outreach is coordinated with distribution, and lessons from loss reasons feed back into pricing and service improvements.

items.name: Communicated to Distribution
items.description: Current appetite is actively distributed to appointed agents and brokers through appetite guides, portal content, and producer meetings so that submission flow matches what the company wants to write. Changes are announced with effective dates, and submission quality metrics are used to confirm the message has landed.

items.name: Documented Appetite by Line of Business, Geography, and Industry
items.description: The appetite statement specifies, for each line of business, the target and acceptable classes, the geographies in which the company will deploy capacity, and the industries it favors, tolerates, or avoids. It is precise enough that an underwriter or broker can determine from the document alone whether a given account merits a submission.

items.name: Exceptions Require CUO Approval with Documentation
items.description: An account on the no-write list may be considered only with the chief underwriting officer's prior written approval, supported by a documented rationale covering the mitigating factors, terms, and pricing that justify the exception. Approved exceptions are logged centrally and reviewed periodically to confirm the conditions of approval still hold.

items.name: Hit Ratio Targets by Segment
items.description: Quote-to-bind hit ratio expectations are set for each target segment and monitored against actuals to gauge competitiveness and submission quality. Hit ratios running well below target prompt review of pricing and terms, while ratios far above target are examined for signs of underpricing or adverse selection.

items.name: No-Write List Maintained and Enforced
items.description: A current list of prohibited classes, operations, geographies, and risk characteristics is owned by the chief underwriting officer's office, published to all underwriters and distribution partners, and coded into clearance and rating systems where possible. Submissions matching the list are declined at clearance, and any prohibited risk found on the in-force book is remediated at the next lawful opportunity.

items.name: Target Classes Defined with Selection Criteria
items.description: For each target market, the department documents the qualifying class codes and the selection criteria that distinguish a desirable account, such as size range, loss history, management quality, and exposure controls. These criteria are used at triage to prioritize submissions and in file reviews to test whether bound accounts genuinely fit the target profile.

items.name: Updated Annually
items.description: The statement is reviewed and reissued at least once a year as part of the planning cycle, incorporating portfolio performance, catastrophe accumulation, reinsurance structure, and market conditions. Material mid-year changes, such as a class restriction following adverse experience, are issued as formal amendments rather than informal guidance.

items.name: Acknowledge Within 4 Hours
items.description: Receipt of a submission is confirmed to the broker within 4 business hours, including the clearance result and the assigned underwriter. The acknowledgment also identifies any information missing against the minimum submission requirements so the broker can cure gaps immediately.

items.name: Declination Documented with Reason
items.description: Every declined submission or renewal is recorded with the specific underwriting reason, such as out of appetite, adverse loss experience, or inadequate information, rather than a generic code. Documented reasons must be permissible under applicable unfair discrimination laws and are retained to support market conduct examinations.

items.name: Decline Letter Within 24 Hours
items.description: Written notice of declination is sent to the broker or applicant within 24 hours of the decision, stating that the company is declining and, where required or appropriate, the basis. Prompt notice preserves the broker's ability to place the risk elsewhere and reflects the service standard the company commits to its distribution partners.

items.name: Firm Quote Within 5 Business Days
items.description: A formal, bindable quote with terms, conditions, and subjectivities is released within 5 business days of a complete submission for accounts the company elects to pursue. Quotes requiring referral or actuarial review remain subject to the same deadline, with delays escalated to management and communicated to the broker with a revised date.

items.name: Indication Within 48 Hours
items.description: For complete, in-appetite submissions, the underwriter provides a non-binding pricing indication within 48 hours, giving the broker an early read on competitiveness. Out-of-appetite submissions are declined within the same window rather than held.

items.name: Minimum Submission Requirements
items.description: A submission is not considered complete and ready for underwriting until it contains a signed application, five years of currently valued loss runs, the line-specific supplemental questionnaire, and a physical inspection where the class or exposure requires one. Incomplete submissions are returned to the broker with the missing items identified, and the service-standard clock starts only when the file is complete.

items.name: No Silent Non-Renewals
items.description: An expiring policy may never simply lapse without an affirmative renewal or non-renewal decision communicated to the broker and insured. Every expiring account must show either issued renewal terms or a compliant non-renewal notice, and aging reports are monitored to catch policies approaching expiration without a recorded decision.

items.name: 40 Hours of Continuing Education Annually
items.description: Every underwriter completes at least 40 hours of qualifying continuing education each year, drawn from industry designations, regulatory courses, and approved internal programs. Completion is tracked centrally, counts toward state licensing CE where applicable, and shortfalls are addressed in the performance review cycle.

items.name: Authority Tied to Competency
items.description: Increases in underwriting or binding authority are granted only on demonstrated competency, evidenced by training completion, audit scores, and file quality, rather than tenure alone. Sustained quality deficiencies can result in authority being reduced until remedial training and supervised file work restore the required standard.

items.name: Technical Training by Line of Business
items.description: Underwriters receive structured technical curricula specific to the lines they handle, covering coverage forms, exposure analysis, rating plans, and emerging risks for that line. New lines of business or significant product changes trigger mandatory training before staff may underwrite the affected business.
